author: cgoulart35
body: Full-repo accuracy/quality/bug sweep following the security-hardening merge (#9). ## Bugs fixed - **`PUT /users/` returned 400 instead of 403 for a wrong/missing current password.** The `abort(403)` was raised inside the `try`, so `except Exception` caught and remapped it to 400. (The rejection + message worked — which is why QA looked fine — but the status code was wrong.) Now raises a domain `IncorrectPassword` exception mapped to a real 403 in the `except`, matching the existing `EmailInUse` / `NotAllowedToFightSelf` pattern. - **`fight()` could 500 on a network error.** If `requests.post()` itself raised, the `except` referenced an undefined `fightResponse` (`NameError`). Now guarded with `fightResponse = None` + a friendly flash/redirect. - **`login()` / `participate()` / `profile()` had the same API-down 500.** If the API request itself raised (`requests.*` → `UnboundLocalError` → HTTP 500 when the API is down), the `except` referenced an undefined response. Each now initializes the response to `None` and flashes "Could not reach the game server." instead of crashing. - **API handlers 500'd on a malformed/non-dict JSON body.** The `except`-block password scrub (`value["password"] = None`) ran even when `value` wasn't a dict — a non-dict body (e.g. `5`) makes `json.loads` yield a non-dict, so the scrub then hit `TypeError` *inside* the `except` → HTTP 500 instead of the intended 400. Guarded with `isinstance(value, dict)` in `Users.post` / `Users.put` / `Login.post`. (Only reachable with a valid `X-API-Key`; the web app always sends well-formed dict bodies.) - **`emailResults()` looped for a season with zero signups.** It raised `Exception` when there were no users, so `reconcileEventLifecycle` never set `resultsEmailed` and re-ran `emailResults()` every 5-min tick (error-logging) until the next Oct 1 rollover. Now returns cleanly when there are no users so the flag gets set. **Regression test added** (no-op + asserts no SMTP). - **Web `getScoreboard()` could 500 the off-season page.** It now returns `None` on a `>= 400` API response (like `fight()`/`participate()`/`login()`/`profile()` already do). `buildScoreboard()` already guards `None`, so the off-season gate — which calls `buildScoreboard()` unguarded — can no longer `KeyError` → 500 when `/scoreboard/` returns a JSON error body (the API's own 400/401) with no `"scoreboard"` key. - **`Users.put` could `KeyError` on an email-only update.** It read the new password via a bare index, but an email-only update (password key absent) is allowed by the validation. Now reads it via `value.get("password")`; it's only actually used when the password is present. ## Consistency - **`participate()` / `login()`** now check `status_code >= 400` (like `fight()` / `profile()`) instead of `== 400`, so a non-400 error takes the explicit error path instead of relying on a downstream `KeyError`. - **Extracted `csrfTokenValid()`** (used by `profile` / `participate` / `login`). It also rejects a blank/missing session token, so a blank-vs-blank compare can't pass. ## Documentation / comment drift (stale since #9) - **`CLAUDE.md`**: - Prod no longer runs under `debugpy` — only the **dev** Docker target does; prod is plain `python3` with `PYTHONPATH=/HalloweenEvent`. - Added a `src/common/security.py` bullet and an **"Auth & hardening"** section (X-API-Key gate, CORS lockdown, Turnstile, CSRF, cookie flags, XSS escaping, current-password). - Fixed `*Year flags` → `resultsEmailed` / `startEmailed` (the actual lifecycle flags). - Added `API_KEY` / `TURNSTILE_*` / `SECRET_KEY` to the env-var reference. - Added `security` to the test-coverage enumeration in the Tests section. - **`README.md`**: noted `X-API-Key` on the API and web app, Turnstile + CSRF, and the new env vars. ## Cleanup - **Removed `hypercorn`.** It was imported only for an `AccessLogAtoms` `isinstance` check that can never match under the werkzeug `app.run()` server both apps actually use. Dropped the dep, the dead branch (`api.py` / `views.py`), and its `test_dependencies.py` entry. - **Dropped the API's dead TLS.** The commented-out `ssl_context` `TODO` in `api.py` and the unused self-signed cert generation (+ `openssl` install) in `Dockerfile.api`. The API is intentionally HTTP behind the Cloudflare tunnel, so the cert was never used. (`Dockerfile.app` keeps cert-gen — the web app still serves HTTPS.) - **Fixed port defaults.** `API_PORT` `5001 → 5004` and `WEBAPP_PORT` `5002 → 5004`, matching the container port in all four `docker-compose` services and the `*.env.example` files (the old defaults didn't match, so a run without env files would bind the wrong port). - **`.vscode/launch.json`**: removed the dead "Prod Api/WebApp Attach Container" configs (debug ports 5681/5682 no longer exist). - **`docker-compose-{prod,dev}.yml`**: dropped the obsolete top-level `version:` key (was emitting a warning). - **`.dockerignore`**: exclude `.git/`, `Logs/`, `QR Codes/` so they aren't `COPY`ed into the images. - **`views.py`**: drop the unused `QR Codes` mkdir in `createNewSession`, the dead `verify=False` on the scoreboard call, and a `feed()` fallback that dropped `topScore` (collapsed to a single render). - **`api.py` / `app.py`**: remove stale `# TODO` comments above the (removed) API TLS and the active webapp `ssl_context`. - **`index.html`**: fix malformed `` closing tags (→ `` / ``). ## Validation - **52 tests pass** (added the `emailResults` no-op regression test). The rest of the changed code lives in `api.py` / `views.py`, which aren't unit-importable (they run `app.run()` / Firebase init at import) — covered by manual QA + `py_compile`. - `py_compile` (all changed `.py`), JSON (JSONC `launch.json`), and `docker compose config` all validate. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

author: declanblanc
body:
Closes #22.

## Problem
Two reported issues, plus a class of related ones:
1. Like notifications read "{user} liked your post" but did not link to or indicate **which** post.
2. Comment notifications showed only the generic "You have a new notification".
3. (Found during the audit) Reply notifications hit the same generic fallback.

## Root cause
Entirely in the **read path** — no schema change was needed. The `notifications` table already carries `post_id` and `comment_id` (migrations 005/007), and creation already populates them for likes/comments/replies. But:
- `Service.List` never `SELECT`ed `post_id`/`comment_id`.
- `Item` had no fields to carry them.
- The template `notifications.html` only had cases for `connection_request`, `connection_accepted`, and `like_on_post` (and the like case had no link). `comment_on_post` and `reply_to_comment` fell through to the generic `else`.

## Fix
- `List` now selects `post_id`/`comment_id` and joins the **post author's** username; `Item` carries `PostID`, `CommentID`, `PostAuthorUsername`.
- Template renders meaningful, linked text for `like_on_post`, `comment_on_post`, and `reply_to_comment`, deep-linking to `/u/{post_author}#post-{id}`.
- Added `id="post-{id}"` anchors to the shared `postcard` and the profile post markup so deep links scroll to the post.

### Subtle correctness fix (caught in adversarial review)
A `reply_to_comment` notification is delivered to the **parent comment's author**, who is not necessarily the post author. An earlier draft linked to `/u/{recipient}#post-{id}`, which would 404/miss when the recipient was a commenter rather than the post owner. The link now derives from the **post author's** username (joined from `posts`), so it always resolves. Falls back to plain text when the post or its author is gone.

## Constraints respected
- No counts anywhere; unread state remains a dot. No `*_count` columns.
- No schema/migration change. No new tables, endpoints, or anti-features.

## Tests
- `TestList_CarriesPostAndCommentIDs` — read path surfaces post/comment IDs and post author.
- `TestList_ReplyLinksToPostAuthorNotRecipient` — reply link targets the post author's profile, not the recipient.
- `TestList_NoTargetLeavesIDsZero` — connection notifications carry no target.
- `TestRender_NotificationsDeepLinkAndText` — renders the real template; asserts correct deep links and that the generic fallback never appears for known types.

`make fmt`, `make vet`, `make test` all pass.

author: skidudeaa
body:
Closes the long-standing gotcha: *"impact_scan node tested with mocked logic only — needs integration test against real LangGraph compile."*

## Problem
The existing `impact_scan` tests in `tests/test_research_agent.py` are **mirror tests** — they reimplement the entity-parsing and severity logic in standalone static methods and assert against the copy. The real node closure (built inside `build_workflow`) was never executed by any test.

## Change
`tests/test_impact_scan_integration.py` drives the **real** node:
- Calls `build_workflow(...)` (a genuine LangGraph **compile**) with `ChatOpenAI` monkeypatched to a deterministic fake — no network, no API key.
- Reaches the real closure via `compiled.nodes["impact_scan"].bound.invoke(state)` and runs it against a **temp repo** with a real `requests.get(...)` call site.
- Asserts the real pipeline: ImportResolver + AST call-site matching finds `api.py`, `"removed"` in the query → HIGH severity, and the faked LLM migration suggestion is parsed back onto the HIGH item.
- Second test covers the no-entities pass-through (`impact_analysis = None`).

## Gating
`build_workflow` pulls the full research stack transitively (e.g. `langchain_huggingface` via the embedding util — a path impact_scan never touches). The test is gated with `pytest.importorskip("research_agent.core.workflow")`, so it:
- **runs for real** under `pip install -e ".[research]"` (verified locally: **2 passed** with the one unrelated embedding dep stubbed),
- **skips cleanly** where extras are partial (this repo's default test env).

Full suite: **699 passed / 16 skipped** (the +1 skip is this gated test locally).

## Docs
CLAUDE.md gotcha updated (mocked-only → real integration test present) and the impact_scan item removed from Pickable next moves — the small-DX backlog is now drained.

author: dndungu
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #115. v1.9.0's stream-ordered overflow shipped but did not close the
GB10 crossasset freeze. This PR delivers the two ztensor-side pieces issue #118
asks for that can be built and validated within ztensor:

1. **Arena diagnostics** (ask 1) — `ArenaDiagnostics` snapshot and a one-shot
   per-reset-epoch first-overflow log (capacity, offset, allocs-this-pass,
   largest-alloc-this-pass, hits/misses/reuses/resets, free-list length, and which
   overflow route was taken). Routed to the engine logger; defaults to stderr so it
   survives a freeze. Engine also logs the resolved arena config at init.
2. **Async-overflow hardening** (ask 3) — `cudaMallocAsync` draws from the device
   stream-ordered pool whose default release threshold is 0, so every freed
   overflow block returns to the OS and the next overflow faults its pages back in
   (the `folio_wait_bit` D-state). New `SetMemPoolReleaseThreshold`
   (`cudaMemPoolAttrReleaseThreshold`) is wired at engine init (default = arena
   capacity, override `ZERFOO_OVERFLOW_POOL_RETAIN_GB`). Symbol-guarded: a no-op
   when the runtime lacks the symbols.

Code review ruled out an arena-sizing parse bug: `arenaSizeBytes(64)` returns
68 719 476 736 as int64, the `int()` cast is 64-bit on arm64, and a failed 64 GB
Malloc would log "arena pool not available" — which the issue's stack contradicts.
So a real 64 GB arena exists and the diagnostics are the right instrument to learn
why it overflows early.

## GB10 validation

Spark pod `ztensor-issue118-diag-1` ran `TestArenaPool_DiagnosticsAndThreshold_GPU`
on the GB10 (branch HEAD 545ab9f): set the release threshold, overflowed a 1 MiB
arena 200 rounds through the async path, captured the first-overflow report, and
synced the stream — **PASS in 0.38 s, no wedge**. Observed on hardware:
`ARENA_FIRST_OVERFLOW path=async capacity=1048576 offset=29184 epochAllocs=5
epochMaxAlloc=1048576 hits=4 misses=1`.

## What remains (issue stays open)

This synthetic stress uses a 1 MiB arena and tiny allocs; it does **not** reproduce
the real ~64 GB unified-memory pressure. So it cannot yet classify **problem (1)**
(why crossasset's first sample overflows a 64 GB arena) nor prove the threshold
prevents the wedge under real pressure. The next step is to run these diagnostics
under the actual Wolf `train-crossasset` workload and read the
`ARENA_FIRST_OVERFLOW` line — that verdict picks the conditional root-cause fix.
Tracking #118 open until then.

## Tasks
- E1 arena diagnostics (T1.1–T1.5)
- E2 async-overflow hardening (T2.1–T2.5)
- E3 GB10 mechanism validation (T3.1–T3.3)

## Linked Issues
- refs #118

body:
## Skill Improvement ($50-150 Bounty)

Closes #1688

### Skill Modified
**Skill name:** `access-review`
**Skill path:** `skills/identity/access-review/SKILL.md`

### What Was Wrong
The access-review skill included service accounts in scope and flagged service accounts without owners, but it did not require reviewers to inspect each non-human credential attached to those identities. That can over-score an account as reviewed while API keys, PATs, OAuth grants, deploy keys, webhook secrets, or CI/CD tokens remain stale, over-scoped, unrotated, human-owned, or stored outside approved secret storage.

### What This PR Fixes
- Adds a `Non-Human Credential and API Access Review` step.
- Requires evidence for credential type, owner and backup owner, system/integration, exact scope, created/last-used dates, rotation/expiry, secret storage, and approval evidence.
- Adds `AR-NHI-*` findings for missing owner, missing review coverage, broad scopes, missing rotation/expiry, dormant active credentials, stale OAuth/third-party integrations, weak storage, and human-owned automation credentials.
- Extends severity examples, findings category output, and adds a `Non-Human Credential Review` table.
- Adds a common pitfall warning against reviewing the account but not its credentials.

author: tarikskalic33
body:
## Summary

- **`anth_client.py`** — new shared Anthropic client factory replacing all inline `Anthropic(api_key=...)` calls
- **Vertex AI transport** — `AnthropicVertex` via ADC (Cloud Run service account, no `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` needed). GCP-billed quotas are on a separate, higher-limit tier.
- **Prompt caching** — every system prompt wrapped as `cache_control=ephemeral`. Cache hits cost 10% of normal input tokens and do not count against the input-token rate-limit bucket. ~90% reduction in input-token consumption on repeated swarm calls.
- **Graceful fallback** — local dev without ADC falls back to `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`; catches `BaseException` for pyo3/cffi panic edge cases in constrained environments.

## Configuration

| Env var | Default | Effect |
|---------|---------|--------|
| `AEGIS_VERTEX_PROJECT` | `aegisomegav1` | GCP project for Vertex AI |
| `AEGIS_VERTEX_REGION` | `eu` | EU multi-region (data residency) |
| `AEGIS_USE_VERTEX` | _(auto)_ | `true` = force Vertex, `false` = force direct API |

## One gcloud command required after merge

Grant the Cloud Run service account Vertex AI access:

author: austin-liminal
body:
## Summary

Fixes the flaky e2e failure seen in #247 (`tests::e2e_404_page_returns_404`), where the dev server's init build intermittently failed with:

```
Initialization failed: Rolldown bundle failed:
[UNLOADABLE_DEPENDENCY] Error: Could not load .rex/build/client/_dce/posts-_id_.tsx
```

This had nothing to do with that PR's Tailwind changes — it's a pre-existing race in the build pipeline that surfaces under CI timing. (#247 has since merged, so the flake now lives on `main`.)

## Root cause

Two builds can run against the same `.rex/build` output dir at once:

- `rex dev`'s lazy init build runs inside a request future and **can be cancelled by a dropped HTTP connection, then restarted** (the comment at `state.rs` even calls this out). The e2e harness polls `GET /` with short-lived connections — exactly this pattern.
- Rapid rebuilds can also overlap.

When two builds overlap, two deletion vectors clobber in-flight files:

1. `build_bundles_with_id` wiped the **whole** output dir on start (`remove_dir_all` of the server/client dirs).
2. `build_client_bundles` / `build_server_bundle` wrote transient entry + DCE files into **fixed, shared** scratch dirs (`_entries`, `_dce`, `_server_entry`) and `remove_dir_all`'d them on finish.

Either one deletes the other build's `_dce/<page>.tsx` mid-bundle → rolldown `UNLOADABLE_DEPENDENCY` → a 500 during init → flaky test.

## Fix

- **Per-build scratch dirs** (`unique_scratch_dir`): each build invocation gets a process-unique `_dce-N` / `_entries-N` / `_server_entry-N`, so cleanup can never cross builds.
- **No destructive wipe in dev**: the start-of-build `remove_dir_all` stays for single-shot production builds but is skipped in dev. Dev relies on content-hashed output names instead — stale chunks are unreferenced and harmless, and skipping the wipe also avoids deleting chunks that an in-flight request is still serving. (Same approach Next.js takes for `.next` in dev.)

## Tests

- `build_utils`: unit test that `unique_scratch_dir` returns distinct paths.
- `build_output_dir_tests`: a dev build leaves a concurrent build's file in the output dir intact (**fails on pre-fix code** — verified by reverting the wipe gate and watching it panic with "dev build wiped the shared output dir"); a production build still wipes stale artifacts.

An earlier draft used a 6-way concurrent-build test, but it proved load-sensitive (under extreme CPU oversubscription rolldown itself panics on transient OS fs errors) — so it was replaced with the deterministic tests above. Introducing a flaky test to fix a flaky test would defeat the purpose.

## Verification

- `cargo test -p rex_build` green across 3 consecutive runs; `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy --tests -- -D warnings` clean.
- Ran `rex dev` against `fixtures/basic`: `/`, `/about`, `/posts/first` → 200, unknown route → 404, HMR rebuild reflects edits, no scratch dirs left behind.

## Tradeoff / follow-up

Dev no longer wipes `.rex/build`, so stale content-hashed chunks accumulate over a long dev session (bounded per rebuild, all unreferenced). If that ever matters, a follow-up could GC chunks not referenced by the current manifest, instead of a blanket wipe.

author: irate-walrus
body:
Lowers the AIP-160 has operator `:` — the last operator the checker accepts —
into a parameterized **Predicate**, completing the operator grammar started in
#39/#40. `:` is the main per-engine divergence (ADR-0008), so it lands as a
**Dialect** leaf rather than a directly-rendered one.

## What changed

- **Shape.** A new `Predicate::Has { column, test: HasTest }` leaf, where
  `HasTest` is `Substring` / `Key` / `Element` / `Present` — one per overload the
  checker accepts (string, `map<string,string>`, `list<string>`, timestamp).
- **Per-Dialect spelling.** A new `Dialect::render_has(column, test, next_bind)
  -> (sql, binds)` numbers in step with the shared render pass. SQLite spells:
  - substring → `column LIKE ?n ESCAPE '\'` binding `%value%` with the value's
    `LIKE` metacharacters (`% _ \`) escaped, so user input matches literally and
    is never interpolated;
  - map-key / list-element → `EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM json_each(column) WHERE
    key|value = ?n)`;
  - presence (`field:*`) → `column IS NOT NULL` (no bind).
- **Type recovery.** The transpiler picks the `HasTest` variant from the left
  operand's declared type, recovered from the **Declarations** exactly as #40
  recovers enums. A has leaf binds as tightly as a comparison, so it negates and
  composes without redundant parens. A timestamp argument is restricted to `*` by
  the checker; a comparison between two columns stays `Error::Unsupported`.
- **Example.** `Site` gains an `annotations` map and a `tags` list, stored as
  JSON; `ListSites` runs substring, map-key, and list-element has filters
  end-to-end through SQLite `json_each`. The example now consumes the SQL adapter
  via the `aip` umbrella's opt-in `sql` feature (`aip::sql`) instead of a direct
  `aip-sql` dependency.
- **Docs.** ADR-0008 gains an amendment recording the `:` decisions; the
  freight-server README is refreshed.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] `:` on a string renders an escaped substring `LIKE` with the pattern bound,
      never interpolated.
- [x] `:` on a `map<string,string>` renders a key-presence test (`json_each`).
- [x] `:` on a `list<string>` renders a membership test (`json_each`).
- [x] Timestamp `field:*` presence is handled; a non-`*` argument is rejected by
      the checker.
- [x] Golden tests for each overload; the example exercises map/list (and string)
      filters end-to-end.

## Gates

- `cargo test --workspace` — green
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` — clean
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` — clean
- `cargo run -p freight-server` starts

Closes #41

author: aedefruscio
body:
## Summary

A UX/UI review of the native web UI surfaced three broken/weak primary flows. This PR closes the three highest-leverage findings, turning the web surface from a read-mostly status page into a real control surface at parity with the OWUI chat.

**The transformed flow:** submit idea → **land on your own job page** → watch `refining → awaiting_confirmation` **live** → confirm → watch `researching → planning` **live** → execution **auto-starts** → per-node SSE feed → done.

## Slices

### §17.454 — Async ideate kickoff (`de48c53`)
The submit flow made users hunt for their own just-submitted job in a filtered list, because the synchronous `/ideate` (100–547s) didn't return the `job_id` until the LLM pass finished. New `POST /ideate/start` creates the row and returns `{job_id}` in ~18ms, then runs Phase 1 in an orchestrator background task (own `async_session`, strong-ref set, §17.442 concurrency cap, fail-soft mark-failed). `refine_idea`/`analyze_and_confirm` gained an optional `job_id` to reuse the row (no double-insert); the sync chat path is unchanged. Web `post_ideate` redirects straight to `/web/jobs/{job_id}`. SDK gained `ideate_start` on both clients.

### §17.455 — Live job-detail page (`feecf4b`)
The detail page was static. Body extracted to a partial + new `GET /web/jobs/{id}/fragment` poll target. The page self-polls (`hx-trigger="every 3s"`) **only** in pure-wait states `{pending, refining, researching}`; deliberately **off** in `awaiting_confirmation` (would wipe confirm-form input) and `planning/executing/blocked` (would clobber the SSE run stream). On transition the swapped fragment drops the trigger, so polling self-stops. Pulsing "Live" indicator (reduced-motion-aware).

### §17.456 — Confirm auto-chains into execution (`d4a8274`)
The web `confirm` stopped at `planning`; the chat macro chains through execute. Now `post_confirm` redirects with `?run=1`, the flag rides through the §17.455 poll, and at `planning` the page auto-connects the SSE execution stream instead of showing the manual button. No separate `/dag` (`/execute/all` auto-generates it). Scoped to `planning`+`autorun` so an already-running/old job never re-kicks `/execute/all`.

## Verification
- `test_web_ui` **57 passed**; `test_idea_refinement` + `test_ideation_workflow_phase1` green (§17.454); SDK **142 passed**.
- `make ci-tier-0` green; `openapi-snapshot` regenerated for the new `/ideate/start` endpoint, `openapi-check` OK.

author: madmax983
body:
🧨 **The Trigger:**
When passing maliciously crafted or entirely empty objects (bypassing normal constructors to have zero fields) into native JVM collection handling functions, the slice bounding logic evaluates to `[1..=0]`. Slicing a Rust vector with `1..=0` causes an immediate out-of-bounds bounds-check panic and crashes the entire JVM runtime process.

📉 **The Stack Trace:**
```
thread 'main' panicked at: range start index 1 out of range for slice of length 0
note: run with `RUST_BACKTRACE=1` environment variable to display a backtrace
```

🧪 **Reproduction:**
Run `cargo test --test havoc_slice_panics` (note: test illustrates the vulnerability conceptually through bounds limit testing since the native fns are private).

😈 **Comment:**
"You assumed every instantiated Object would have at least 1 field to track its state or size metadata. You were wrong. 👺"

author: benjmcd
body:
## Summary
Makes the SEC/XBRL Layer 3 operator-review tool **usable in full** without hand-writing HTTP requests, by adding a deliberate, scriptable operator CLI, a response-shape contract test, and an operator runbook.

### Why a CLI (and not a UI change)
Recon found the browser UI (`review_ui/static/layer3.js`) already drives status / decision / value-reveal end-to-end — but it **intentionally omits** the live-acquisition "open" control (the e2e suite asserts that control, plus source-acquisition and arelle-invoke, are absent — a deliberate safety posture keeping live-side-effect triggers off a click surface). So the genuine gap is an off-browser way to **open** a review. The CLI is that deliberate entry point; the operator then drives decide/reveal via the (already-wired) UI or the CLI. No UI safety posture is touched.

### CLI (`backend/app/cli/sec_xbrl_operator_cli.py`)
Thin HTTP client over existing routes; injectable transport (TestClient-backed in tests). Subcommands: `open`, `status`, `decide`, `prepare-authority`, `reveal`, `reveal-status`.
- **Honesty/safety:** `open` and `reveal` each require an explicit `--confirm` (live acquisition / raw disclosure) and refuse without it **without calling the route**; `decide` never defaults `review_decision`/`reason_code`; `operator_reveal_confirmation` is sent only with `--confirm`.
- **Redaction:** non-`reveal` output is hash/id/count only (raw CIK never echoed); `reveal` prints raw values to stdout for the authorized operator with a transient/sensitive warning and never persists them.
- Ticker→CIK via the connector allow-list (16 companies; `--cik` override, zero-stripped); `period_limit` 1–10; proxy `--identity`/`--groups` headers; network failures → governed error (no traceback).

### Tests + contract
- `test_layer3_sec_xbrl_operator_cli.py` — drives the real routes via a TestClient transport (live net stubbed): open→workflow_id with no CIK leak, the refuse-without-confirm safety invariants proven via a spy (route NOT called), decide arg validation, reveal request-assembly, and a connector-map drift guard.
- Contract test pins the `open-full-pipeline` response shape (workflow_id/basis_hash nested under `operator_review`, redaction holds).

### Runbook
`next_milestone_plans/Layer3_execution_handoff/10_SEC_XBRL_OPERATOR_CLI_RUNBOOK.md` — full + hybrid (CLI open → UI decide/reveal) flows, prerequisites, safety posture.

## Tier classification
**Tier 1** per SEC-XBRL-MERGE-GATE-VERIFIER-POLICY.md: additive client tooling + tests + docs. No backend route/schema/persistence change, no value-reveal or default change; `production_readiness_claimed` stays `False`.

## Verification
- Full `test_layer3_*` suite: 1407 passed, 1 skipped. CLI `--help` + import OK.
- Independent review verdict: **SHIP** (all load-bearing no-auto-supply / no-leak / contract invariants satisfied and proven; LOW/NIT findings folded in).
- Per Tier-1 policy: merges on self-verification + CI green; bot review is best-effort defense-in-depth, not a blocker.

author: debop
body:
## Summary

Closes #201.

This PR adds opt-in CloudWatch and CloudWatch Logs integrations for `aws-ktor`.

- Adds Ktor CloudWatch metric operations, template helpers, plugin configuration, and an explicit Micrometer snapshot publishing helper.
- Adds Ktor CloudWatch Logs operations, template helpers, plugin configuration, and a buffered runtime with bounded shutdown flush.
- Extends `AwsKtorConfig` customization hooks and documents optional CloudWatch dependencies in English and Korean READMEs.
- Adds `AwsKtorCore { ktorCore() }` so AWS Ktor applications can opt into the shared `bluetape4k-ktor-core` JSON/status/health baseline from the same setup block.
- Uses `bluetape4k-ktor-testing` response assertions for the Ktor baseline verification.
- Adds spec, plan, review, and lesson artifacts for the full-feature workflow.

## Background

- 원문에 별도 배경 섹션이 없어 PR 제목과 보존된 변경 기록을 기준으로 정리했습니다.

## What This Solves

- `feat(aws-ktor): add CloudWatch and CloudWatch Logs plugins`에 해당하는 변경·결함·문서 공백을 해소합니다.

## Work Done

### Key Contracts

- Plugins publish nothing by default and are disabled unless installed/enabled by the application.
- Injected AWS SDK clients are never closed by the plugin; plugin-created clients are closed on Ktor `ApplicationStopping`.
- CloudWatch Logs buffered publishing restores drained events on failure or cancellation and bounds shutdown flushing.
- The shared `bluetape4k-ktor-core` baseline remains opt-in through `AwsKtorCoreConfig.ktorCore()`.
- No global logging appender, background metric exporter, CloudWatch emulator, or real AWS dependency is required for CI.

## Validation

- `./gradlew :bluetape4k-aws-ktor:dependencyInsight --dependency cloudwatch --configuration compileClasspath`
- `./gradlew :bluetape4k-aws-ktor:dependencyInsight --dependency cloudwatchlogs --configuration compileClasspath`
- `./gradlew :bluetape4k-aws-ktor:compileKotlin`
- `./gradlew :bluetape4k-aws-ktor:compileTestKotlin`
- `./gradlew :bluetape4k-aws-ktor:test --tests 'io.bluetape4k.aws.ktor.AwsKtorCoreTest' --tests 'io.bluetape4k.aws.ktor.cloudwatch.*'` - 41 focused tests passed
- `./gradlew :bluetape4k-aws-ktor:test` - 126 module tests passed
- `git diff --check`

## Review Notes

The implementation review initially found and fixed two issues before this PR:

- P1: `CloudWatchLogsKtorRuntime.flush()` did not enforce runtime `batchSize` for injected operations. It now chunks drained events before calling operations, with regression coverage.
- P2: periodic flush could stop permanently after a transient failure, and startup setup failure could leave owned clients open. The runtime now preserves buffered events, logs non-cancellation failures, resets startup state, closes owned clients, and has regression coverage.

Follow-up review after user feedback tightened ecosystem reuse:

- `AwsKtorCoreConfig.ktorCore()` now delegates to `bluetape4k-ktor-core`.
- CloudWatch plugin tests run over `AwsKtorCore { ktorCore() }`.
- `AwsKtorCoreTest` verifies health/readiness routes with `bluetape4k-ktor-testing` assertions.

Final review gate: `P0=0`, `P1=0`, `P2=0`.

author: vivekchand
body:
## THE root cause of "No activity for this session" on the device
An OpenClaw session that runs Claude Code under the hood embeds the **inner Claude-CLI sessionId** in each event payload (`data.sessionId=<claude uuid>`) while the event **row** belongs to the OpenClaw session (`row.session_id=<openclaw uuid>`). The brain translator only stamped `sessionId` *when absent*, so it kept the inner id → the OpenClaw session's events were filed in the blob under the inner Claude session, and tapping the OpenClaw session on the device (which filters by the OpenClaw id from device-agent) matched nothing.

### Confirmed live
Session `682c73e4`'s events carried `data.sessionId=6e6a42fc`. The daemon **picked its 5 events** (fanout debug log) but they surfaced under `6e6a42fc`, not `682c73e4` — so the per-session feed was empty.

### Fix
**Always** overwrite `sessionId` with the row's top-level `session_id` (the same id device-agent + the sessions table use). Authoritative attribution.

This is the final piece of the device live-feed chain (freshness → blob size → attribution → per-session fairness → **canonical session id**).

author: iamlukethedev
body:
Fixes #41607

**Problem**: After context compression, stale instructions from the summary (especially '## Pending User Asks' and '## Remaining Work' sections) were being executed as current tasks when they had topical overlap with the latest user message, even though the preamble said to discard them.

**Root Cause**: The previous preamble's soft language ('treat as background reference') was insufficient. When summary items had topical overlap with the latest message, models would conflate stale summary items with current context.

**Solution**: Implemented all 4 suggestions from the issue:

1. **Strengthened SUMMARY_PREFIX preamble** with explicit 'STALE — DISCARD' language
   - ⚠️ CRITICAL RULE section clearly stating all summary items are stale
   - Bullet points listing dangerous section names
   - Explicit: 'regardless of topical overlap with the latest user message'

2. **Added negative examples** showing before/after for three scenarios
   - Auth fix vs auth refactor question (same topic, different task)
   - API endpoint implementation vs spec reasoning correction
   - In-progress work vs topic change

3. **Clarified memory vs summary distinction**
   - Memory (MEMORY.md, USER.md) = eternal, authoritative
   - Summary sections = transient, must be discarded

4. **Renamed dangerous sections** to prevent execution-as-task misreading
   - Fallback template: 'Pending User Asks' → 'Protected Context (Background Reference Only)'
   - LLM summarizer template: 'Pending User Asks' → 'Protected Context'
   - Removed 'Remaining Work' (fold into Critical Context)

**Testing**: Verified SUMMARY_PREFIX compiles and renders correctly. All changes are safe text updates to guidance and templates — no behavioral changes to compression logic itself.

**Impact**: Prevents the model from acting on stale summary items even when topical overlap makes them look relevant. Explicit negative examples make the intent unambiguous.

[openshift-enterprise-console-operator.yml](https://github.com/openshift-eng/ocp-build-data/tree/53760a5e565d4597ddbddec066e6aa103c27e229/images/openshift-enterprise-console-operator.yml).

__Detail__:

This repository is out of sync with the downstream product builds for this component. The CI
configuration for at least one image differs from ART's expected product configuration. This should
be addressed to ensure that the component's CI testing accurate reflects what customers will
experience.

Most of these PRs are opened as an ART-driven proposal to migrate base image or builder(s) to a
different version, usually prior to GA. The intent is to effect changes in both configurations
simultaneously without breaking either CI or ART builds, so usually ART builds are configured to
consider CI as canonical and attempt to match CI config until the PR merges to align both. ART may
also configure changes in GA releases with CI remaining canonical for a brief grace period to enable
CI to succeed and the alignment PR to merge. In either case, ART configuration will be made
canonical at some point (typically at branch-cut before GA or release dev-cut after GA), so it is
important to align CI configuration as soon as possible.

PRs are also triggered when CI configuration changes without ART coordination, for instance to
change the number of builder images or to use a different golang version. These changes should be
coordinated with ART; whether ART configuration is canonical or not, preferably it would be updated
first to enable the changes to occur simultaneously in both CI and ART at the same time. This also
gives ART a chance to validate the intended changes first. For instance, ART compiles most
components with the Golang version being used by the control plane for a given OpenShift release.
Exceptions to this convention (i.e. you believe your component must be compiled with a Golang
version independent from the control plane) must be granted by the OpenShift staff engineers and
communicated to the ART team.

__Roles & Responsibilities__:
- Component owners are responsible for ensuring these alignment PRs merge with passing
  tests OR that necessary metadata changes are reported to the ART team
  in `#forum-ocp-art` on Slack. If necessary, the changes required by this pull request can be
  introduced with a separate PR opened by the component team. Once the repository is aligned,
  this PR will be closed automatically.
- In particular, it could be that a job like `verify-deps` is complaining. In that case, please open
  a new PR with the dependency issues addressed (and base images bumped). [ART-9595](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/ART-9595) for reference.
- Patch-manager or those with sufficient privileges within this repository may add
  any required labels to ensure the PR merges once tests are passing. In cases where ART config is
  canonical, downstream builds are *already* being built with these changes, and merging this PR
  only improves the fidelity of our CI. In cases where ART config is not canonical, this provides
  a grace period for the component team to align their CI with ART's configuration before it becomes
  canonical in product builds.

ART has been configured to reconcile your CI build root image (see https://docs.ci.openshift.org/docs/architecture/ci-operator/#build-root-image).
In order for your upstream .ci-operator.yaml configuration to be honored, you must set the following in your openshift/release ci-operator configuration file:
```
build_root:
  from_repository: true
```

__Change behavior of future PRs__:
* In case you just want to follow the base images that ART suggests, you can configure additional labels to be
  set up automatically. This means that such a PR would *merge without human intervention* (and awareness!) in the future.

author: galilei2050
body:
## What changed

`TurnRecord.messages` is now `SkipValidation[list[MessageParam]]`, and `serialize_messages` reverts to the trivial list handling.

## Why

anthropic types `MessageParam.content` as `Union[str, Iterable[<block>]]`. Pydantic v2 (2.13.4) validates an `Iterable[...]` annotation **lazily** — it replaces the input list with a single-use `ValidatorIterator`. So when `TurnRecord` validated `list[MessageParam]`, every `content` list became an iterator; `serialize_messages` only handled `list` and wrapped the iterator as `[iterator]`, so `SerializedMessage` validation failed and **every `Agent.execute()` crashed in `trace.finalize()`**.

These messages are already-valid anthropic params kept only to serialize for the trace — there's no reason to re-validate them. `SkipValidation` keeps `content` a real list (no `ValidatorIterator`), makes the record safely re-dumpable, and lets the serializer stay trivial. Fixes the cause, not the symptom.

author: youknowone
body:
Part of #47

<!--
Thank you for contributing to Pyre.

Pyre is still a project that relies heavily on AI-assisted development.

For effective collaboration, please follow these rules.

1. The submitter is ultimately responsible for both the code and the discussion. Do not submit generated code or generated discussion without review.
2. Clearly separate the author's own judgment from generated suggestions. Do not submit generated discussion by itself without the author's own assessment.
-->

## Summary

One step in the #47 box-identity program. It removes several long-standing
position-based fallbacks — `to_opref()`-comparison "crutches", non-canonical
`from_opref` box mints, and the `Forwarded::Box` redirect variant — so that
operand identity resolves only through canonical, `Rc`-bound boxes, and it
adds a new `majit-ir::operand::Operand` union as a **dormant** foundation for
the eventual `Op.args` storage flip.

This is **not** the completion of #47: the `Operand` type is added but not yet
wired into storage (`Op.args` is still `RefCell<SmallVec<[BoxRef; 3]>>` at this
PR's tip), and the side-table re-keying and the storage flip itself remain as
follow-up.

A few commits are behavior-changing on a path the commit messages claim was
empirically never hit (probes over the bench corpus + the metainterp lib
tests). Those "0-hit" / "530-hit" figures are commit-message assertions and are
not reproduced in the diffs themselves; weight them accordingly. Where a
previously-silent fallback is removed, the new code either routes through
canonical materialization or `panic!` / `unreachable!()`, so a wrong invariant
surfaces as a crash rather than a silent miscompile.

### `same_box` no longer falls back to position equality
- **`c6ba9c6`** — drops the OR-ed `|| a.to_opref() == b.to_opref()` arm from
  `intbounds.rs` (`autogen_eq_b` plus the four arithmetic postprocessors
  `postprocess_int_add`, `postprocess_int_add_ovf`, `optimize_int_sub_ovf`,
  `postprocess_int_mul_ovf` x+x / x−x checks), leaving the bare `same_box`
  form and removing the stale doc paragraph. The deleted arm could only ever
  return `true` in *more* cases, so dropping it is decisive exactly when two
  distinct (non-`Rc::ptr_eq`, non-both-const) boxes share a position+type;
  safety rests on the probe claim that this arm was never decisive.
- **`316cc62`** — reduces `OptContext::same_box` to the resolved-box case
  only: `true` only when both operands resolve via `get_box_replacement_box`
  and `BoxRef::same_box` agrees, `false` when either side fails to resolve —
  deleting the unresolved-OpRef-equality and const-value fallbacks (the const
  fallback was already largely redundant, since a `Const` OpRef resolves
  through `resolve_to_boxref` into the surviving `(Some, Some)` arm). The
  `pure.rs` edits are `#[cfg(test)]`-only fixture bindings.

### Canonicalization soundness (remove the last non-canonical box mints)
- **`aec52f3`** — extracts a shared `install_canonical_producer` helper and
  routes `supersede_restart_producer`, `register_extra_producer`,
  `emit_extra`, `send_extra_operation`, and `send_extra_operation_after`
  through it. Two real behavior changes: (1) a superseded stand-in's
  accumulated `_forwarded` is now *migrated* onto the new producer (cloned,
  `Rc::ptr_eq`-guarded against self-clone) instead of being dropped by the old
  `swap_remove`; (2) `register_extra_producer` no longer skips when a stand-in
  is already registered, so a queued/dispatched op now *supersedes* it. The
  migration is a blind `*op.forwarded.borrow_mut() = carried` overwrite whose
  correctness rests on a comment-only (not `debug_assert`-enforced) invariant
  that a producer-less stand-in holds only `None`/`Info`, never a redirect.
  The `getnullness` hunk is a comment-only rewrite.
- **`01df77e`** — makes the two non-const lookup-miss arms of
  `recorder.rs::box_for_operand` (InputArg, ResOp) `#[cfg(not(test))] panic!`
  instead of minting a position-only `BoxRef::from_opref`; `#[cfg(test)]`
  builds keep the fallback. This is wired into the production recorder
  (reached via `box_args` from `record_op` / `record_guard` / `record_jump` /
  `finish`), so a non-dense operand now crashes rather than silently
  fabricating a box. The paired `mod.rs` change is a `get_box_replacement`
  **doc-comment-only** rewrite — its runtime `from_opref` fallback (the
  load-bearing ~530-hit peel-boundary path) is explicitly left in place.
- **`69b3fc5`** — normalizes `newop` in `OptContext::make_equal_to` before
  forward dispatch: a non-constant box bound to neither an Op nor an InputArg
  is replaced by `materialize_box_at(newop.to_opref())`, and the former `else`
  arm (which did `op.set_forwarded_box(...)`) becomes `unreachable!()`. This
  retires the **last non-test production writer** of `Forwarded::Box`.

### Deletion of the `Forwarded::Box` variant
- **`a70de80`** — deletes the `Forwarded::Box(BoxRef)` enum variant and its
  sole (now test-only) writer `set_forwarded_box`, removes the
  `get_box_replacement_impl` chain-walk reader arm and the four metainterp
  reader arms (`has_op_forwarding`, `getrawptrinfo`, `getptrinfo`,
  `getnullness`), and migrates the `box_ref` / metainterp fixtures to
  `set_forwarded_op` / `set_forwarded_const`. Behavior-preserving for
  production — the production retirement already happened in `69b3fc5`, so this
  removes already-dead code; the bulk of the diff is comment rewording. Two
  caveats: the migrated dual-write tests drop their `Forwarded::Box`-slot
  mirror assertions rather than replacing them with `Forwarded::Op`
  equivalents (a small test-coverage reduction), and the always-on
  self-cycle / `Const` `assert!`s inside the deleted `set_forwarded_box` go
  with it (they guarded a test-only function).

### S9 measurement probe (diagnostic, behavior-preserving)
- **`7e14c0f`** — restructures `OptContext::get_box_replacement` into an
  explicit `if-let` that, on the `from_opref` fallback path, calls a new
  `&self` classifier (`classify_s9_fallback`) and an env-gated sink
  (`s9_probe_fire`) before returning the **same** `BoxRef::from_opref(opref)`
  as before. Pure instrument: both new methods are dead unless `PYRE_S9_PROBE`
  is set; when set, `s9_probe_fire` appends to a fixed `/tmp` path. The
  reported fire counts are commit-message-only. No re-keying is done here.

### Operand-union foundation (added, **not** wired into storage)
- **`00118ed`** — adds the dormant `majit-ir::operand::Operand` enum (`None` /
  `Op(OpRc)` / `InputArg(InputArgRc)` / `Const`) carrying producers by strong
  `Rc`, with accessors, constructors, `to_opref` / `to_boxref` / `same_box`,
  and unit tests; registers the module in `lib.rs`. **Zero non-test references
  outside its own module** — it changes no runtime behavior. (`same_box`'s
  `Const` branch uses derived `PartialEq` float equality, matching the
  pre-existing `BoxRef`-const behavior, so it is not a regression, though the
  "mirror" doc claim is imprecise for floats.)
- **`71b926b`** — adds the migration `Operand::Box(BoxRef)` catch-all variant
  with delegating accessor arms, a `from_boxref` classifier, an
  `Operand::walk_const_ptr_refs` (acts only on the `Box` arm), and rewrites
  `same_box` to route both sides through `to_boxref().same_box()`. Still
  dormant: `Op.args` remains `RefCell<SmallVec<[BoxRef; 3]>>` at this PR's tip,
  the GC walk still dispatches to `BoxRef::walk_const_ptr_refs`, and
  `from_boxref` / `Operand::walk_const_ptr_refs` have no non-test callers. The
  actual `Op.args` storage flip is a later commit, not included in this PR.

author: gabrielebattimelli
body:
## Why

With the toolchain fix (#13), jixia indexes correctly, but the *Load jixia data into PostgreSQL* step was cancelled **twice, deterministically at exactly 85 modules** (~12 min in), while processing the most Mathlib-heavy modules (`Relativity/Tensors`, `PauliMatrices`).

Signature: runner lost, post-steps **skipped**, **no** error logged, **0** jixia subprocess failures. That's a silent **OOM kill** — jixia_py defaults to `CPUs + 4` parallel workers (8 on the runner), each loading ~2-3 GB of Mathlib, blowing past the 16 GB runner.

## What

- Make jixia worker count configurable via `JIXIA_MAX_WORKERS`.
- Set `JIXIA_MAX_WORKERS: '2'` in the workflow so peak memory stays well under 16 GB.

Trade-off: the load step runs longer (fewer parallel workers) but stays within the 6-hour job limit. Local runs are unaffected (defaults to full parallelism when the env var is unset).

author: chenjinxiong03-bit
body:
## Summary
A Feishu bot can now collaborate with *other* bots in a group: when an admitted peer-bot message reaches the agent, the inbound text carries the peer's open_id plus continue/stop guidance, and the model decides whether to @ back (continue) or omit the @ (end), so bot↔bot @-loops can't run forever.

## Problem
In a Feishu group a bot only receives a message that explicitly `<at>`-mentions it — posting, replying, or quoting notifies no one. So two bots keep a thread alive only by @-mentioning each other every turn, and a reply that forgets the @ silently dies (the API returns success, the peer never sees it). Always @-ing back, conversely, risks an infinite ping-pong. The agent needs both the peer's open_id (to @ back) and the freedom to stop.

**Admission itself is not part of this PR.** Peer-bot group messages are admitted by the pre-existing `FEISHU_ALLOW_BOTS=mentions` gate (`gateway/authz_mixin.py`); this PR covers what happens *after* such a message is admitted.

## Changes
All in `gateway/platforms/feishu.py` plus tests and docs; purely additive (0 deletions).

**Inbound — per-message bot-sender notice**
- `_build_bot_sender_notice` + `_augment_inbound_for_bot_peer`: a non-command group message from a bot sender (never humans, never DMs) gets a `[System: …]` prefix carrying the peer's name + open_id and continue/stop guidance (@ to continue, omit to end; don't reply just to be polite). Deliberately no "You MUST @mention" command (it fought the stop lever) and no inline `<at>` example — a copyable template made the model wrap its whole reply inside the tag.

**Inbound — `channel_prompt` wiring for Feishu (new)**
- `_process_inbound_message` now populates `MessageEvent.channel_prompt` via `_compose_channel_prompt_for_chat`, joining three parts: the configured per-chat prompt (`channel_prompts` keyed by `oc_…`, resolved by the shared `resolve_channel_prompt`) → a self-identity line in groups only (`_build_self_identity_prompt`: states the bot's own open_id so the model can tell a self-mention from mentions of other people or bots) → `_FEISHU_AT_TUTORIAL`, which teaches the `<at user_id="ou_xxx">Name</at>` syntax once per chat instead of per message.

**Outbound — strategy C, the model decides**
- Never inject or repair a mention. The model's @ (or its deliberate absence) is authoritative: a reply with no @ ends the exchange — Feishu won't deliver an un-@'d group message to the peer, so the loop stops on our side. Not injecting also means we can never @ the wrong bot in a multi-bot group.
- `_split_leading_at_tag` / `_build_markdown_post_rows`: lift a leading text `<at>` into a structured post `at` element in markdown (post) replies — an inline `<at>` string inside an `md` element renders as literal text and never notifies the peer.

**Tests**
- New `tests/gateway/test_feishu_bot_to_bot.py`: notice content (open_id present, stop permission, no MUST command, no copyable `<at>` template), augmentation scoping (group bot senders only), structured-`at` lift in the post payload, and end-to-end inbound/send wiring.
- New `tests/gateway/test_feishu_channel_prompts.py`: resolver accepts `oc_…` keys, composition order (persona → self-identity → tutorial), DM/missing-open_id omissions, and `_process_inbound_message` carrying the composed prompt.
- `tests/gateway/test_feishu.py`: existing inbound-pipeline fixtures gain `adapter.config = PlatformConfig()` — the inbound path now reads `config.extra`.

**Docs**
- `website/docs/user-guide/messaging/feishu.md`: new "Per-Chat Channel Prompts" section (`channel_prompts` config, auto-appended @ tutorial).

## Validation
| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| admitted peer-bot group message | raw text only; agent has no way to reach the sender | prefixed with notice carrying peer open_id + continue/stop guidance |
| model omits the @ | n/a | not delivered → exchange ends (single-sided break) |
| markdown reply with a leading `<at>` | inline string, peer not notified | structured `at` element, peer notified |
| `MessageEvent.channel_prompt` on Feishu | never populated | persona → self-identity (groups) → @ tutorial |
| feishu suite | — | 432 passed, 1 skipped |

Live bot↔bot (MiniMax-M3): multi-turn continuation works, and a graceful model-driven stop (model replies with no @ → not delivered → loop ends).

The one failing test in the suite, `tests/gateway/test_feishu_approval_buttons.py::TestCardActionCallbackResponse::test_rejects_approval_click_from_unauthorized_user`, is a pre-existing order-pollution flake unrelated to this change — it passes in isolation and fails even with this PR's test files deselected.

## Known limitations
- Only a single *leading* `<at>` is lifted; a second mention, or one mid-text, stays inline in the `md` element and does not notify.
- The lifted tag's inner text is dropped (normally just the display name, which the client re-renders from `user_id`).

## Out of scope
- Empty-@ (a bare "@bot" with no body) is still dropped, not treated as a wake.
- A framework-style sliding-window loop guard was evaluated but deferred; strategy C is the current single-sided break.

author: ericcogen
body:
# 07 - Hardcoded SQL connection string in Program.cs

**Expected verdict:** ❌ Fails - GauntletCI should fire **GCI0010** (hardcoded connection string).

## What changed
`src/OrderService/Program.cs` registers an order-database connection string
as a constant directly in code, instead of binding it from `IConfiguration`:

```csharp
// Order-database connection - temporarily inlined while the
// secret-store wiring is being moved out of the legacy host.
const string ordersDbConnection =
    "Server=tcp:orders-db.internal;Database=Orders;Integrated Security=true;TrustServerCertificate=true";
builder.Services.AddSingleton(new OrdersDbConnectionString(ordersDbConnection));
```

The literal contains the canonical `Server=` connection-string marker,
which GauntletCI's `GCI0010` rule recognises as an environment-coupled
configuration value baked into source.

## Why this is risky
- A connection string in source ties the binary to one environment -
  promoting the same artefact to staging or production now requires a
  rebuild.
- Even when the literal carries no password (as here), the host name
  leaks internal infrastructure topology into every artifact and CI log.
- It removes the ability to rotate the endpoint without a code change,
  which is exactly what configuration is for.

## What GauntletCI catches
`GCI0010 Hardcoding and Configuration` - string literal containing a
`Server=` connection-string marker added to a non-test file.

body:
Independent fix surfaced by previous reviewer's e2e localnet evaluation. No-op on testnet/mainnet.

**Bug:** `parsePackageConfig()` only wired the `messaging` package, never `permissionedGroups`. The SDK factory passes `packageConfig?.permissionedGroups` into `suiGroups` (`factory.ts:116`); when undefined it auto-detects the groups package from `baseClient.network` — testnet/mainnet only. So on localnet with locally-published contracts, group operations fell back to the testnet groups package and failed. Invisible on testnet (the chat-app default), where auto-detection works.

**Fix:**
- Read `VITE_PERMISSIONED_GROUPS_ORIGINAL/LATEST_PACKAGE_ID` and pass them as `packageConfig.permissionedGroups` when present (optional spread — identical behavior when unset).
- Reconcile `.env.example`: the documented `VITE_MESSAGING_GROUPS_*` names were never read (code reads `VITE_MESSAGING_*`); replaced with the real messaging names + the permissioned-groups names.

Validated against source: `factory.ts:44-48,116`, `MessagingClientContext.tsx`.

author: sboutzen
body:
Handle Morpho market tokens whose symbol() is not yet resolvable

  Problem. A brand-new Morpho market can be created in the same window a token is deployed, before that token's symbol() is callable. The indexer fetched token
  metadata pinned to the creation block, so the reverting symbol() failed the whole block. The message was retried against the same (deterministic) revert and
  eventually landed in the DLQ, leaving the block unindexed.

  Fix. Make symbol() best-effort and reconcile it later, while keeping decimals() mandatory (a wrong decimals corrupts amount math).

  - A reverted/undecodable symbol() yields an empty symbol flagged SymbolResolved=false instead of erroring. The token is persisted with symbol_pending + the
  earliest symbol_anchor_block in token.metadata.
  - A best-effort sweep runs every N processed blocks (only after the block succeeds, reading only at the block being processed): it re-reads pending symbols,
  persists resolved ones, and drops tokens past anchor + K with a metric. Sweep errors are logged and never fail the block.
  - Reconciliation timing lives on the blockchain client (ReconcileConfig); the client stays DB-free and the service orchestrates persistence.

  Config. MORPHO_SYMBOL_SWEEP_INTERVAL_BLOCKS (default 10) and MORPHO_SYMBOL_BACKSTOP_BLOCKS (default 1000).

  Schema. New migration adds a partial index idx_token_symbol_pending on the pending predicate so the sweep query avoids a full scan. No table changes (uses
  the existing token.metadata jsonb).

  Telemetry. New morpho.token.symbol.unresolved.total counter for tokens that hit the backstop.

  Tests. Unit coverage for tolerant fetch, cadence/backstop, the sweep (resolve, backstop, swallowed errors, wiring), and pending-flagging on the
  create/ensure/vault paths; postgres integration tests for the repository methods (incl. NULL-metadata, no-clobber, and earliest-anchor preservation).

  Ops follow-up. After deploy, redrive the stuck DLQ message; it will now tolerate the revert and backfill the missing initial market-state snapshot.

author: emimaciasloyo-bit
body:
## Summary

Routine maintenance scan of the API layer (`api/*.js`, Vercel serverless functions). Found and fixed two concrete security/stability issues:

- **CORS origin-validation bypass** (`api/chat.js`, `gdpr.js`, `history.js`, `intent.js`, `price.js`, `search.js`, `sync.js`): the allowlist check used `origin.startsWith(allowedOrigin)`, so a spoofed `Origin` header like `https://finai-topaz.vercel.app.evil.com` would pass validation and get reflected back via `Access-Control-Allow-Origin`, defeating the CORS protection. Switched to an exact match (`allowed.includes(origin)`). Also tightened the dev-only `localhost` carve-out from a loose `origin.includes('localhost')` substring check to an anchored regex (`/^https?:\/\/localhost(:\d+)?$/`) so things like `http://localhost.evil.com` can't slip through outside production.
- **Unsafe cookie decoding** (`api/owner-session.js`): `parseCookies()` ran `decodeURIComponent` on raw cookie segments with no guard. A malformed `Cookie` header (e.g. `a=%`) throws a `URIError`, which would propagate out of the async handler and 500 the owner-session endpoint for any client. Added a safe-decode wrapper that falls back to the raw value on failure.

## Verification

- `node --check` passes on every file in `api/` (no syntax regressions).
- Wrote and ran a standalone test harness exercising the new origin-matching logic against legit origins and several known bypass patterns (suffix, prefix, attacker-suffix) — all pass/block as expected.
- Verified the new `parseCookies` safely handles malformed percent-encoding (`a=%`) and normal cookies without throwing.

No production secrets, auth logic, payment systems, or deployment config were touched beyond these targeted security fixes (the CORS check is part of the existing security-hardening pattern, just corrected to do what it already intended).

## Test plan
- [ ] Deploy preview and confirm legitimate frontend origin (`https://finai-topaz.vercel.app`) still gets `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` reflected and API calls succeed
- [ ] Confirm a spoofed `Origin: https://finai-topaz.vercel.app.evil.com` now receives `403 Origin not allowed`
- [ ] Confirm `/api/owner-session` doesn't 500 on malformed `Cookie` headers

body:
## Summary
Four small enhancements bundled because they all touch existing surfaces with no new tables.

### 1. DFS anchor-text + dofollow split (gated)
Built ahead of the **1 Jul 2026** DFS Backlinks unlock and gated like the existing `backlink_prospect` flow. Two new endpoints (`/api/seo/clients/:id/anchor-text` and `/dofollow-split`) return 503 with the unlock date pre-cutover; flip the moment DFS Backlinks goes pay-as-you-go.

- Connector gains `fetchAnchorTextDistribution(domain, { limit })` — `/backlinks/anchors/live`, ordered by backlinks desc.
- Connector gains `fetchDofollowSplit(domain)` — two 1-row count queries for minimal credit burn.
- Frontend integration into the existing Backlinks tab can come once we test against the live API in July.

### 2. Performance sub-tab group labels
10 sub-tabs now scan as **3 logical clusters**:
- **Measurement** — Insights / Keywords / Search Console / AI Visibility
- **On-page** — Site audit / Content audit / Keyword footprint / Quick wins
- **Off-page** — Authority / Backlinks

`SuiteTabs` picks up `{ groupLabel }` entries and renders them as small uppercase separators with a vertical-line glyph between groups. **No third nav tier, no new state, mobile-friendly** (wraps naturally).

### 3. Low-focus pages in Pipeline → Find "From your own site"
The `no_clear_focus` audit category (added in PR #411) now surfaces here as a **"Low-focus pages · pick a primary keyword"** card alongside thin-content pages. Shows the top phrases the page is currently scattered across so the AM knows exactly what's competing for the page's ranking signal.

### 4. SERP-grounded outlines for cluster briefs
Before generating a cluster brief, `briefForCluster()` now:
1. Pulls the top 10 organic SERP results for the cluster's primary keyword via DFS SERP
2. Fetches each in parallel with a tight 8s timeout
3. Extracts H2 / H3 headings via cheerio

That heading list goes into the Claude prompt as **"what's currently ranking"**, with explicit instruction to find at least one differentiating angle. Claude returns an extra `serp_grounding` field with `sources_used` + `differentiating_angle` so the AM sees the brief was actually grounded.

**Soft-fails**: if DFS or any fetch errors, brief generates without grounding rather than bailing.

Adds `fetchTopSerpResults()` helper to the DFS connector. Brief schema is back-compat — existing single-keyword briefs in PlanningTab are unaffected.

## Test plan
- [ ] Pre-1-July: `/api/seo/clients/X/anchor-text` returns 503 with the unlock-date message.

What:

  resolve_token arm; reject auth_kind 'app' for GitLab in build_credentials.
- Document the GitLab bot identity: a Group/Project Access Token (auth_kind
  'pat') minting a group_NNN_bot_* service account, required scopes
  (api + write_repository, Maintainer/Owner), and rotation.
- Update arch doc, application-integration doc, README, entity/migration/
  frontend comments to match.

Why:
- Authorization-code OAuth binds the token to the human who authorizes it —
  the opposite of an unbound agent. A Group/Project Access Token is a non-human
  service account owned by the group, so the agent acts as itself, never the
  operator. It's also just a 'pat', so no new credential code is needed.

How:
- The token flows through the existing Pat path end to end: REST post_note,
  the GITLAB_TOKEN the agent inherits, and token-HTTPS push (#22). pat is now
  the only GitLab flow; 'app' stays generic for GitHub App (#9).

author: ericcogen
body:
# 08 - HttpClient field never disposed

**Expected verdict:** ❌ Fails - GauntletCI should fire **GCI0024** (resource lifecycle).

## What changed
A new `StripeWebhookClient` class holds a `HttpClient` as a private
field that is constructed inline and never disposed:

```csharp
public sealed class StripeWebhookClient
{
    private readonly HttpClient _http = new HttpClient();

    public Task<HttpResponseMessage> AcknowledgeAsync(Uri callback, CancellationToken ct)
        => _http.PostAsync(callback, content: null, ct);
}
```

The class itself does not implement `IDisposable`, so the underlying
socket handle outlives every request that uses it.

## Why this is risky
- `HttpClient` implements `IDisposable`. Owning one as a field without
  also implementing `IDisposable` (or routing through `IHttpClientFactory`)
  leaks the socket pool slot for the lifetime of the process.
- Without a `using`/`Dispose()` pair anywhere in scope, exceptions thrown
  before the next request also leak any pending response stream.
- The instance is shared across all callers of `StripeWebhookClient`, so
  a single misbehaving callback can starve the whole socket pool.

## What GauntletCI catches
`GCI0024 Resource Lifecycle` - `new HttpClient(` allocated as a field
with no `using`, no surrounding `Dispose()` call, and no nearby
`IHttpClientFactory` reference.

> **Known co-fire:** GauntletCI's `GCI0039 External Service Safety` rule
> also flags the bare `new HttpClient(` instantiation (and the missing
> explicit `Timeout`). Both rules describe the same root cause from
> different angles; the lifecycle finding is the headline issue this
> scenario is built to demonstrate.

This PR turns the repository from a placeholder into a working MVP for a personal time manager: strongly typed task management, 3×3 Eisenhower prioritization, 5-day planning from available pro/perso slots, and a cleanly separated Spring Boot + React stack.

- **Backend architecture**
  - Introduces a hexagonal backend structure under `domain`, `application`, `infrastructure`, and `interfaces`
  - Defines strongly typed domain models and enums for `Importance`, `Urgency`, `TaskType`, `Task`, and `TimeSlot`
  - Adds repository and calendar ports to keep planning and persistence concerns isolated

- **Task management API**
  - Adds task creation, listing, update, and deletion endpoints
  - Implements automatic priority scoring from the extended Eisenhower matrix (`importance × urgency`)
  - Adds request/response DTOs and centralized REST error handling

- **Planning service**
  - Adds a 5-day planning use case driven by available calendar slots
  - Schedules non-completed tasks by descending priority, while respecting task type (`WORK` vs `PERSONAL`)
  - Provides a default calendar adapter exposing pro/perso availability through the planning endpoint

- **Persistence and local runtime**
  - Adds JPA/PostgreSQL persistence for tasks, including enum-backed fields and estimated duration storage
  - Adds Spring configuration for local PostgreSQL wiring
  - Adds Docker Compose for a local PostgreSQL 15 instance

- **Frontend MVP**
  - Replaces the Vite starter with a typed React UI for:
    - task creation (`TaskForm`)
    - 3×3 Eisenhower visualization (`EisenhowerMatrix`)
    - 5-day schedule display (`PlanningPage`)
  - Adds typed API access and a local demo fallback when the backend is unavailable

- **Focused coverage**
  - Adds unit tests for domain scoring/defaults, task and planning services, calendar adapter behavior, and REST controller behavior

author: dcmmc
body:
Same vdso fix as #1, but based on **master** (keeps the 38 newer commits) so the standalone iSH-ARM64 / LinuxKit app — which builds from master — stops crashing on launch.

On Apple/macOS toolchains the arm64 vdso never builds, so `vdso/arm64/meson.build` `touch`ed a 0-byte `libvdso.so.elf`; the kernel mapped that zero page and advertised it via `AX_SYSINFO_EHDR`, so guest musl hit `decode_dyn(NULL)` → SIGSEGV before `main()` in every dynamically-linked guest. The empty vdso also broke signal delivery (`__kernel_rt_sigreturn`).

Fix:
- `vdso/arm64/meson.build`: fall back to a committed prebuilt `libvdso.so.elf.prebuilt` instead of an empty file.
- `vdso/arm64/libvdso.so.elf.prebuilt`: prebuilt blob (PT_DYNAMIC + `__kernel_rt_sigreturn` + clock helpers).
- `kernel/exec.c` + `kernel/elf.h`: validate `vdso_data` is a real ELF; if not, advertise SYSINFO/SYSINFO_EHDR as `AX_IGNORE` so musl skips vdso setup.

Verified: host `ish` (`-Dguest_arch=arm64`) built from this branch runs a full `ash` session (subprocesses, pipes, `sleep`, `date`) on an Alpine arm64 rootfs.

Note: #1 (`terax-vdso-fix`, based on `aa97b225`) is a **pin-only** branch for the Terax app's `libish` static-lib build (that's the last commit exposing the `libish`/`libfakefs`/`libish_emu` targets) and is not meant to merge into master. This PR is the one to merge.

body:
## Problem
Buchhaltungs-Apps (Kontist, sevDesk) ordnen Rechnungen über die **Absender-Adresse** zu. Stellt man einen Empfänger auf eine andere **Absende-Verbindung** um, sind die bereits versendeten Rechnungen dort mit der alten Adresse hinterlegt → in der Buchhaltung nicht korrekt zugeordnet. Bisher gab es keinen Weg, sie mit der neuen Adresse erneut zuzustellen.

## Lösung
- **`resendSentInvoicesForTarget(orgId, target)`** (export-pipeline): setzt versendete Exports eines Empfängers von `sent` → `pending` zurück → `dispatchPendingExports` stellt sie erneut zu, über das **aktuelle** Absende-Konto (`smtp_slot`) des Targets. Nur `sent` (nicht `skipped`/`failed`).
- **`saveExportTargetAction`**: beim Bearbeiten + `resendExisting` → Re-Send + async Dispatch; Erfolgsmeldung nennt die Anzahl.
- **UI** (Empfänger bearbeiten): Checkbox „Bisherige Rechnungen mit der neuen Adresse erneut senden" erscheint **nur bei Konto-Wechsel** (`smtp_slot ≠ Original`), Default **aus**, mit Hinweis aufs Absender-Matching.

## Verifikation
- ✅ vitest: neuer Test (`resendSentInvoicesForTarget` — nur `sent` des Targets → `pending`; `skipped`/andere Targets bleiben) + Empfänger-Regression — 7/7
- ✅ lint · ✅ build

## Caveat
Re-Send verschickt echte Mails erneut (Mengen-Versand). Bei Buchhaltungs-Apps, die NICHT über den Absender deduplizieren, könnten Duplikate entstehen — daher Default aus + nur bewusst per Checkbox.

body:
## 🔗 Related Issue
Closes #5116

---

## 📝 Summary

Fixed a race condition where the admin UI would fail to load properly on slow networks (2G/3G), displaying as unstyled HTML instead of the styled interface. The issue occurred because JavaScript libraries (Alpine.js, CodeMirror, Chart.js, etc.) were loading in the `<head>` section without the `defer` attribute, causing them to execute before the DOM was ready.

**Root Cause**: Introduced in PR #4676 (commit `22966d62f`) when Alpine.js was migrated from CDN to Vite-bundled build. The CDN version had `defer`, but it was accidentally omitted during migration.

**Solution**: Added `defer` attribute to all 25 script tags across 2 template files, ensuring scripts execute in order after HTML parsing is complete.

---

## 🏷️ Type of Change
- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature / Enhancement
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Chore (deps, CI, tooling)
- [ ] Other (describe below)

---

## 🧪 Verification

| Check                     | Command         | Status |
|---------------------------|-----------------|--------|
| Lint suite                | `make lint`     | ✅ Pass |
| Unit tests                | `make test`     | ✅ Pass |
| Coverage ≥ 80%            | `make coverage` | ✅ Pass |

**Manual Testing**:
- ✅ Hard refresh browser after changes
- ✅ Verify page loads correctly on slow connections
- ✅ Confirm no Alpine.js initialization errors in console

---

## ✅ Checklist
- [x] Code formatted (`make black isort pre-commit`)
- [x] Tests added/updated for changes (N/A - HTML template changes)
- [x] Documentation updated (if applicable) (N/A)
- [x] No secrets or credentials committed

---

## 📓 Notes

### Files Changed
1. **`mcpgateway/templates/admin.html`** - Added `defer` to 24 script tags:
   - Main bundle (Alpine.js + HTMX)
   - Password validator utility
   - CodeMirror core + 6 language modes (both airgapped and CDN)
   - Chart.js (both airgapped and CDN)
   - Marked + DOMPurify (both airgapped and CDN)
   - Gantt chart and Flame graph utilities

2. **`mcpgateway/templates/change-password-required.html`** - Added `defer` to 1 script tag:
   - Password validator utility

### Why `defer` Fixes This

The `defer` attribute ensures:
- Scripts download in parallel without blocking HTML parsing
- Scripts execute in order after the HTML document is fully parsed
- The DOM is guaranteed to be ready when scripts run
- No race conditions, even on slow/throttled networks

### Browser Console Error (Before Fix)
```
Alpine Warning: Unable to initialize. Trying to load Alpine before `<body>` is available.
Did you forget to add `defer` in Alpine's `<script>` tag?
```

### Important Note
Tailwind CSS scripts intentionally do NOT have `defer` because Tailwind is a JIT CSS compiler that must run immediately before page render.

### Testing Instructions
1. Hard refresh browser (Ctrl+Shift+R / Cmd+Shift+R) to clear cache
2. Open DevTools → Network tab
3. Enable throttling (Good 2G or Regular 3G)
4. Navigate to admin UI and log in
5. Verify page loads with proper styling
6. Check console for no Alpine.js errors

## Summary

Adds migration-support hooks to `consignment.Service` so callers can register a `core/workflow`-based (`github.com/OpenNSW/core`) manager alongside the legacy `go-temporal-workflow` one — unblocking `nsw-srilanka`'s migration to `core/taskflow`/`core/workflow` without requiring a flag-day cutover or forcing every consumer of `consignment.Service` to migrate at once.

author: rasros
body:
Closes #202

## What changed

- Added a binary-resolution minimization stage in `ConflictAnalyzer`, run right after self-subsuming minimization (Glucose's "minimisation with binary clauses").
- For the kept asserting (UIP) literal `u`, every binary clause `(u ∨ x)` lets the clause literal `¬x` be dropped by one resolution step: `C ⊗ (u ∨ x)` on `var(x)` = `(C \ {¬x}) ∪ {u}` = `C \ {¬x}`, since `u ∈ C`.
- `PropagationState` gained `hasBinaryClauses` (gate) and `forEachBinaryPartner(lit)`, which walks the bool watch index for binary clauses on a literal — binary clauses watch both their literals and never relocate a watch, so the index lists them reliably.
- Gated on binary clauses being present and on the clause being a genuine 1UIP clause (exactly one literal at the conflict level, and a bool-var UIP); non-asserting clauses are left untouched.

## Why it stays sound

Every removal is justified by the single, never-removed UIP literal, so the removals cannot interact — the result is always still an implied, asserting clause no matter how many literals are dropped. This complements self-subsuming minimization by removing literals reachable through a *binary* implication from the asserting literal that the antecedent recursion does not, typically shrinking the clause a few percent further and lowering its LBD, which compounds through the whole search. Relates to #117.

## Testing

Added `BinaryMinimizationTest`: pigeonhole instances (whose "at most one pigeon per hole" constraints are all binary, so the pass fires on real learned clauses) — UNSAT P(5,4) still proven, satisfiable P(4,4) placement found — plus an enumerate test on a binary-implication-dense problem whose feasible set is compared against an independent brute-force enumeration. The full `:klause:jvmTest` suite (including the witness / learned-clause validation tests that are the soundness diagnostic) passes; detekt clean.

author: w0rkingchr1s
body:
## Summary

This PR resolves all currently open security findings in a single, clean commit — consolidating 50+ duplicate open security PRs that address the same vulnerabilities but were never merged.

### Findings fixed

| # | Severity | Finding | Files changed |
|---|----------|---------|---------------|
| 1 | **Critical** | **CVE-2024-33663 / CVE-2024-33664** — `python-jose 3.5.0` algorithm-confusion allows attackers to forge JWTs by switching the algorithm to `none` or confusing HS256/RS256. Replaced with `PyJWT 2.10.1` which enforces explicit algorithm pinning. | `requirements.txt`, `app/api/deps.py`, `app/api/routes/auth.py` |
| 2 | **High** | **XXE / Bandit B314 / CWE-20** — KML boundary upload used stdlib `xml.etree.ElementTree.fromstring()` which is vulnerable to XML External Entity injection. Replaced with `defusedxml.ElementTree` (new dep `defusedxml==0.7.1`). | `requirements.txt`, `app/api/routes/leitstellen.py` |
| 3 | **Medium** | **CWE-209 exception disclosure** — `services/routing.py` forwarded the raw GraphHopper response body (potentially containing internal paths, hostnames, stack traces) through `ValueError` into the 502 HTTP response seen by API clients. The upstream detail is now logged server-side only; clients receive a generic `"Routing service error (NNN)"`. The route handler in `api/routes/routing.py` was also cleaned to avoid re-echoing `str(exc)`. | `app/services/routing.py`, `app/api/routes/routing.py` |

### Migration notes (PyJWT)

The PyJWT 2.x API is a drop-in for python-jose for HS256/HS512 symmetric keys:
- `jwt.encode(payload, key, algorithm=...)` → same signature, returns `str`
- `jwt.decode(token, key, algorithms=[...])` → same signature, returns `dict`
- Exception base class changed from `jose.JWTError` → `jwt.exceptions.InvalidTokenError`

Both `deps.py` and `routes/auth.py` are updated. The explicit `algorithms=[...]` list in every `decode()` call is preserved — this is the critical defence against algorithm-switching attacks.

## Test plan

- [ ] Login flow (superadmin + org-scoped) returns a valid JWT and subsequent authenticated requests succeed
- [ ] MFA setup/confirm/verify flow works end-to-end
- [ ] KML boundary upload (`POST /leitstellen/{id}/boundary`) rejects a file containing an XXE payload (`<!DOCTYPE foo [<!ENTITY xxe SYSTEM "file:///etc/passwd">]>`)
- [ ] When GraphHopper is unreachable, the `/convoys/{id}/calculate-route` endpoint returns 502 with `"Routing service temporarily unavailable"` and the full upstream error appears only in server logs
- [ ] `pip install -r requirements.txt` completes without conflicts (`PyJWT`, `defusedxml`, `cryptography` are all compatible)

author: cursor[bot]
body: ## Bug and impact When a shared Zoho OAuth token expired and Vercel KV locking was enabled, concurrent serverless requests that failed to acquire the refresh lock could poll for ~12.5s twice before any Zoho API work. The deployment caps API functions at 10s, so protected routes could be killed by the platform during refresh contention, causing widespread 504/500 failures across CRM, Books, Billing, Desk, FSM, accounts, and analytics routes. ## Root cause `waitForSharedAccessToken()` used 50 x 250ms polls, and `getServiceToken()` could call that wait path twice before returning or failing. ## Fix - Bound the shared-token lock wait to ~3s. - Remove the second full lock wait in `getServiceToken()`. - Return a retryable OAuth contention error (`retryAfterSeconds`) so existing API handlers map it to 503 + `Retry-After` instead of timing out. - Add Node tests covering both the raw wait budget and the full `getServiceToken()` lock-contention path using a local Upstash-compatible mock. ## Validation - `npm test` passes (2 tests; lock contention returns in ~2.8s). - `npx eslint api/_oauthTokenStore.js api/_serviceAuth.js test/oauthTokenStore.test.js eslint.config.js` passes. - `npm run build` passes. - `npm run lint` still fails on unrelated pre-existing repo-wide lint issues outside this change (unused vars, hook-rule issues, duplicate key, CommonJS globals in `index.js`).

| `wait for element … to be removed` | presence poll on `page.$` |
