author: yxtay
body:
## Summary
- Tune rclone mount flags to fix Sonarr VideoFileInfoReader getting stuck on debrid file reads
- Root cause: `--buffer-size 0` disabled memory buffering + `--vfs-read-ahead 1G` caused excessive prefetch per file open
- Remove unused flags (`--links`, `--use-cookies`)
- Enable persistent VFS cache via `--cache-dir`

## Changes
| Flag | Before | After | Reason |
|------|--------|-------|--------|
| `--buffer-size` | 0 | 64M | Restore memory buffering |
| `--vfs-read-ahead` | 1G | 64M | Reduce prefetch to prevent hang |
| `--vfs-read-chunk-size` | (default 128M) | 4M | Smaller initial chunks for fast first-byte |
| `--vfs-read-chunk-size-limit` | 1G | 32M | Cap chunk doubling |
| `--vfs-read-chunk-streams` | 4 | removed | Use sequential mode, fewer HTTP connections |
| `--dir-cache-time` | 1m | 5m | Restore default, reduce API calls |
| `--attr-timeout` | 10m | 1y | Debrid files immutable after creation |
| `--cache-dir` | (none) | /config/rclone/cache | Persistent cache survives restarts |
| `--links` | set | removed | Unused for WebDAV |
| `--use-cookies` | set | removed | Unused for WebDAV basic auth |

## Test plan
- [ ] Deploy and verify Sonarr no longer hangs on VideoFileInfoReader
- [ ] Confirm rclone mount healthy after restart
- [ ] Check VFS cache persists across container restarts

body:
## Summary

Makes the Talk sentence engine fully functional across every supported language, closes the usage-learning loop, adds user-added vocabulary with per-user learning and board filtering, and fixes the iOS app falling into offline mode.

### Sentence engine (all languages)
- **Learning loop wired**: nightly cron now actually runs; learned + curated transition weights are read at request time to rank suggestions (the table was previously write-only); clicks blend into scores (capped so usage dominates without erasing the AI prior).
- **AI prediction fixed**: compact `[id,prob]` output + `maxTokens` 3000 reliably returns 50 words; truncated responses are salvaged instead of discarded.
- **All 13 locales seeded** (en/de/es/fr/nl/pt/it/mt/ja/zh/ko/ar/hy) — 295 words / 24 templates each, per-language grammar — via a new `generate-talk-seeds` tool with a `--check` CI gate; dev deploy applies every seed.

### User words + board filter + per-user learning
- New `/v1/sentence/words` endpoints to add/list/delete custom words (e.g. a name like "Sil"), owner-scoped (IDOR-safe).
- `vocabulary?q=` board search; custom words merge in and resolve inside sentences/saved phrases.
- Per-user affinity: a word added at a position returns there next time, and a user's own picks reorder their suggestions without touching the shared model.
- Web client wired with filter input + "Add …" affordance.

### iOS fix
- DEBUG build pointed at `dev-api.tikotalks.com` (the generation zone) instead of the sentence worker's `dev.sentence.tikoapi.org`, so every request 404'd into offline fallback. Pointed dev at the correct host.
- Stopped rendering the "Offline limited mode" banner twice.

### Testing
- 113 Talk tests (engine behavior + all-locale pack validation) + the full `tests/` contract suite (275) green; repo typecheck clean.

Note: the generated `apps/talk/ios/TikoTalk.xcodeproj/` is intentionally not committed (XcodeGen artifact).

author: dong-qiu
body:
Fourth sub-PR of the #46 series. Per `docs/issue-46-plan.md` §4, this
batch ports `frame_cm_interface` (92 fns / 364 .data rows — single-file
largest of the interface_tlcp series). 95% of the C TC families test
`HITLS_*` runtime accessors on a constructed connection that the Rust
port folds into `TlsConfig` builder set-time, or omits as plan §6
out-of-scope (`GetClientVersion` / `GetCurrentCipher` / `GetState` /
`GetRwstate` / `GetReadPending` / `GetRandom` / `GetFinishVerifyData` /
`Set/GetEndpoint` runtime / `Set/GetSigalList` runtime / UIO / PSK
`SetPskClient`/`FindSession`/`UseSession` / `SetTmpDh` /
`SetDhAutoSupport` / `SetEcPointFormats`). The remaining builder fields
that `test_config_builder_*` already pins (`enable_encrypt_then_mac`,
`send_fallback_scsv`, `post_handshake_auth`, `record_size_limit`,
`max_fragment_length`, `ticket_key`, `max_early_data_size`,
`psk_server_callback`) are scope-cut here.

Real gap: 13 builder fields not yet pinned by any round-trip test.

25 new tests appended to
`crates/hitls-tls/tests/migrated_interface_tlcp_audit.rs` (all default):

- `cipher_server_preference` default on + off round-trip (2)
- `flight_transmit_enable` default on + off round-trip (2)
- `quiet_shutdown` default off + on round-trip (2)
- `session_id_context` default None + bytes round-trip (2)
- `security_level` default 1 + level round-trip + `security_cb`
  install (3)
- `heartbeat_mode` default 0 + round-trip (2)
- `middlebox_compat` default on (RFC 8446 §D.4) + off round-trip (2)
- `empty_records_limit` default 32 + round-trip (2)
- `psk_identity_hint` round-trip (1)
- Callback install pins (`msg_callback` / `info_callback` /
  `record_padding_callback` / `cookie_gen+verify_callback` (combined) /
  `client_hello_callback` / `dh_tmp_callback` / `ticket_key_cb`) — 7

Codifies a new methodology pattern:

**Callback-install pin = None→Some discrete flip**. When a unit test
can't drive a handshake to actually fire the callback (would need
`TcpStream` + full handshake loop), pin only the install-side `Option`
discriminant. Trade-off: deleting a builder fn → compile error;
mutating the `Option` internals → test still passes but no production
semantics. Acceptable as documented limitation — strictly better than
"no install-side coverage" without paying for "install + drive
handshake + verify cb fires" in a unit test.

Plan-doc updates: §4 has T198 row ticked + T197 delivered count
corrected to 11 (was placeholder).

Validation:
- `cargo test -p hitls-tls --all-features --test migrated_interface_tlcp_audit`:
  **57/0** (T195 11 + T196 10 + T197 11 + T198 25; incl. 2 TLCP-gated).
- `cargo test -p hitls-tls --test migrated_interface_tlcp_audit`:
  **55/0** (default feature).
- `cargo test -p hitls-tls --tests`: **1114 + 55 + 6 / 0** — zero
  regression.
- `cargo fmt --check` + `cargo clippy --workspace --all-features
  --all-targets -D warnings` clean.

Refs #46 (4 of 5 sub-PRs)

body:
Implements the merged v0.29 proposal (#61, ADR 0058) — an **extension-only** increment that makes v0.28's semantic tokens actually colour in the editor, plus a Karn-specific inlay-hints toggle. No `karnc`/server/language change.

## vscode-karn

- **`contributes.semanticTokenTypes`** — `capability`/`service`/`agent`/`provider`, each with a standard **`superType`** (`interface`/`type`/`class`/`function`) so modern semantic-highlighting themes colour it. **`semanticTokenModifiers`** — `refined`/`opaque`/`platformNative`. **`semanticTokenScopes`** — TextMate fallbacks (e.g. `capability → entity.name.type.interface`; the Karn-distinctive modifier combos → `support.type`) so even non-semantic themes colour them. v0.28's tokens now render out of the box.
- **`karn.inlayHints.enable`** via a `provideInlayHints` middleware that returns `[]` when off (no server change). README documents it as the persistent per-language preference, with `editor.inlayHints.enabled` (instant toggle) and `editor.semanticHighlighting.enabled` as the built-ins.

## karn-lsp

- **`tests/legend_drift.rs`** — the one enforceable cross-component contract: parses `vscode-karn/package.json` and asserts its declared custom token types/modifiers equal `semantic_tokens_legend()`'s custom entries (legend minus the LSP-standard `type`/`function`/`declaration`). One source of truth (the Rust legend), order-independent set comparison. **`exclude`d from the published crate tarball** (`Cargo.toml`) since it reads a sibling file outside the package; still runs in-repo via `cargo test --workspace` (verified absent from `cargo package --list`).

## Docs & process

Spec §3.14 client-theming note; ADR 0058 + index row; changelog row; version bumped to 0.29.0; proposal deleted.

## Validation

`cargo test --workspace`, `clippy -D warnings`, `fmt --check`, the extension's `tsc --noEmit` + `vsce package` (schema-validates the new `contributes`), and the book build + linkcheck are all green. The actual rendered colours are theme-dependent (not auto-testable) — the contract test guards the names; colours are a manual check.

### Release note
Under the single-version posture this is the **first OIDC publish** — when v0.29 releases, watch the `publish-crates` job and keep the `CRATES_REGISTRY_TOKEN` secret until it's green. The four crates republish at 0.29.0 with effectively unchanged source (the drift test is excluded from `karn-lsp`'s tarball), which crates.io permits.

body:
## Overview
This pull request introduces a comprehensive suite of features, performance optimizations, and user experience enhancements aimed at positioning Monize as a robust replacement for desktop personal finance software like Quicken.

## Core Features Implemented

### 1. Balance History Chart Enhancements
* **Timeframe Presets**: Added report-style timeframe selector buttons (`1M`, `3M`, `6M`, `1Y`, `YTD`, `All Time`, `Custom`) directly to the Balance History chart header, operating independently of the transaction table list.
* **Fast Render Toggle**: Added a slide switch to dynamically toggle downsampling mode (saving preference to localStorage).
* **Backend Query Downsampling**: Dynamically downsamples database results (weekly for ranges > 1 year; monthly for ranges > 3 years) when Fast Render is active, keeping cumulative balances 100% correct by calculating the daily running balances inside a PostgreSQL CTE before downsampling.

### 2. Custom AI Import Instructions & Coercion
* **Encrypted Instructions**: Users can specify custom AI processing instructions for transactions parsed via the Smart Import tool (securely stored in the database using the app-wide encryption key).
* **Account Type Coercion**: The AI-assisted transaction parser now dynamically coerces imported account types to match the destination account type.

### 3. AI Smart Import Feature
* **Natural Language Parsing**: Copy-paste raw bank statement text, transaction receipts, or CSV-like dumps and parse them using OpenAI's LLM engine.

### 4. Paycheck Wizard & Category Auto-seeding
* **Paycheck Setup Wizard**: A multi-step wizard to set up recurring paychecks with automatic gross pay, deductions, tax withholdings, and net deposits.
* **Category Auto-seeding**: Auto-populates standard paycheck-related categories (e.g. Gross Salary, Federal Tax, Health Insurance) during user onboarding.

### 5. Split Transaction Enhancements
* **Collapse Splits**: Added a user interface function to collapse split transactions back into regular, single-category transactions.

### 6. Tax Line Support
* **Tax Line Assignment**: Added tax-related metadata tracking fields to Categories to match Quicken's schedule-tax grouping feature.

### 7. Support for New Account Types (Phase 1)
* **Expanded Accounts Schema**: Added support for additional specialized accounts (e.g. Brokerage, Asset, and Liability accounts) in the transaction import wizard.

---
## Verification & Testing
* **Backend Tests**: Verified query parameter parsing, dynamic date bounds resolution, and database interval query correctness (`npm run test -- src/accounts/accounts.service.spec.ts`).
* **Frontend Tests**: Verified interactive renders, loading states, and callback behaviors (`npx vitest run BalanceHistoryChart.test.tsx`).

Both scripts now require `MAESTRO_DEVICE_ID_IOS` and fail fast with a clear message (Android keeps the standard `emulator-5554`). *(prior H11)*

Selectors verified against `crucially-mobile/lib`:

Duplicated device/app-id resolution across scripts; composer/assert/refresh sequences duplicated across 14 flows; `appId` re-declared per flow; `ensure_feed` order-dependence; Android-only `back` run on iOS; placeholder flows reported as US coverage; dead `config/maestro.yaml`; hardcoded sleeps; silent-fail data reset; stale README; no chat-create/billing/offline coverage.

author: sinh-x
body:
## Summary

`droid exec --auto -f <primerPath>` avoids passing 110KB primer text as a command-line argument, which causes the old interactive `droid` TUI to hang forever waiting for user input.

## Root Cause

The old v0.1.50 binary used `droid -m <model> <primer>` (interactive TUI) instead of `droid exec --auto -m <model> -f <primer>` (non-interactive). The `-f` flag reads the primer from a file, preventing the shell from truncating or misinterpreting the massive argument.

## Change

- adapter.ts: `args.push(primer)` → `-f opts.primerPath` in foreground exec path
- 1 line changed in droidcode-pa

## Verification

```
typecheck: pass | test: 310/310 pass
```

body:
## What changed
- add transient learner-overlay x-axis dragging so the learner pitch path can be aligned without moving playback, the model graph, or mutating recorded analysis data
- reset learner alignment when fresh target or learner graph data is rendered, and expand render duration for positive offsets so rightward drags do not clip the learner path
- extend focused coverage across renderer, integration, and end-to-end tests for zoom, selection preservation, playback, blur, pointer cancel, lost pointer capture, and viewport-bound dragging

## Why
The learner comparison overlay was hard to use because there was no way to visually align a user's recording against the model without changing the underlying recording or hijacking other graph interactions. The follow-up review also exposed a real renderer bug: positive learner offsets could push the overlay past the current duration and clip the tail.

## Impact
Users can now drag only the learner pitch overlay to compare timing while preserving normal cursor scrubbing, selection gestures, and playback behavior. The alignment remains transient, which keeps stored recording data canonical and avoids backend or persistence changes.

## Validation
- `npm run test -- editor-inline.visualizer-renderer.test.ts`

author: akpdeepak
body:
## What & why

The frontend `security-audit` gate started failing on `main` and **every open PR** when two `esbuild` advisories published:

- **GHSA-gv7w-rqvm-qjhr** — missing binary integrity verification → RCE via `NPM_CONFIG_REGISTRY` (high)
- **GHSA-g7r4-m6w7-qqqr** — dev-server arbitrary file read on Windows (high)

Both cover esbuild `0.17.0–0.28.0`. It was pulled in **transitively** (deduped) by Vite 8 and Storybook 10 at `0.27.7` — nothing in the app depends on it directly, so this is unrelated to any feature work; it just trips `npm audit --audit-level=high` repo-wide.

## Fix

A single npm `overrides` entry pins esbuild to the patched **0.28.1** across both dependency trees. This is deliberately **not** `npm audit fix --force`, which would have downgraded Storybook to 8.6.18 (a breaking devDependency change).

```json
"overrides": { "esbuild": "0.28.1" }
```

## Verification

- `npm audit --audit-level=high` → **0 vulnerabilities** (was 2 high).
- `npm ls esbuild` → `0.28.1` resolved for Vite, Storybook, and `@storybook/csf-plugin` (all deduped/overridden).
- Toolchain unaffected: **Vite build**, **Vitest 455/455**, and **storybook build** all pass.

Rule books: 10 (§12 dependencies — security advisory remediation; lockfile committed), 40 (§4 dependency/security scanning in CI).

author: chaoming0625
body:
## Summary

Rebuilds the two static-delivery NEST synapses as frozen parameter specs + pure `update(state, ctx) -> (new_state, w_eff)` kernels on the cluster-01 `EventPlasticProj` substrate, retiring their eager `ImperativeSynapseBase` implementations. Both are **delivery-semantics** models (no learned weight evolves) — this **closes the non-plastic `EventPlasticProj` delivery family** (`static`, `static_synapse_hom_w`, `bernoulli`, `cont_delay`).

### `bernoulli_synapse` — static + stochastic transmission
- Per-edge Bernoulli gate on the delivered amplitude: `jax.random.uniform(ctx.key, (E,)) < p_transmit`. The shape-`(E,)` draw gives **edge-axis independence** from the substrate's single 0-d step key (JAX threefry counter PRNG: output `j` ← counter `j`) — so two edges from one pre and multapses gate independently, and **no per-edge `split`/`fold_in` seam is needed**.
- No substrate change.

### `cont_delay_synapse` — static + sub-dt (continuous) delay
- Adds an **additive, default-off** substrate seam `fractional_delay`: deliver the binary event at the integer floor delay, then split the post amplitude across the two bracketing grid steps with a one-step FIR `[1−frac, frac]` (built in `init_state`, where `dt` is known). Charge + arrival centroid exact; `frac==0` (integer delay) collapses byte-identical to a grid delay.
- Default-off via `getattr(rule, 'fractional_delay', False)` → zero risk to existing rules. Output-side split is required because `BinaryArray` binarizes the pre vector.

## Parity (live NEST 3.9.0)

| check | result |
|---|---|
| bernoulli `p=1` ≡ static | exact (CAT_B V_m trace) |
| bernoulli `p=0` | flat at rest |
| bernoulli `0<p<1` | seed-mean V_m within CAT_D 5% (6 seeds, E=20 multapse drive) |
| cont_delay integer/grid delay | exact (CAT_B), verified first |
| cont_delay sub-dt vs precise `iaf_psc_exp_ps` | ∫V_m + EPSP peak match ~1e-4 rel; peak timing ±1 step (CAT_E); onset transient (~0.25 mV / ~4.3 mV EPSP) documented as an intrinsic grid-integrator residual |

## Tests & coverage
- NEST-free `*_rule_test.py` for both specs — **100% line coverage** each.
- Live-NEST `_validation/*_parity_test.py` for both.
- Substrate seam unit-tested **default-off** in `_event_plastic_test.py`.
- Regression: **331 NEST-free tests passed** across clusters 01/04/05/07 + the simulator (the seam is zero-risk).
- Eager `*_test.py` deleted; Lessons entry appended to `CONTEXT.md`.

author: ishou
body:
## Workstream
W2 (implementation) of the **B'/amend convergence** fix for the breaking-bump plan loop (ADR-0068 amendment, spec `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-13-breaking-bump-b-amend-loop-design.md`, merged in W1 #859).

## Why
The helm v3.21.0→v4.2.1 live test burned all 6 B↔C rounds → `needs-human`, because `b_round(N+1)` downloaded C's findings but **not its own `plan-round(N)`** — so Agent B regenerated from scratch each round and silently dropped prior coverage.

## What ships
- **`scripts/breaking-bump/plan.py`** — pure `assert_monotonic(prev, new)` = `entries(prev) − entries(new) − accounted_removals(new)`, strict over `dispositions` keys **and** every `a`/`b`/`c` entry; drops allowed only via `_amendments.removed{entry,reason}`. Tolerates malformed plans without raising.
- **`b_round2…6`** in `breaking-bump.yml` — each now downloads its `plan-round(N-1)` → `./plan.json`, copies it aside to `prev-plan.json` before Agent B runs, then a **monotonicity guard step** (`::error::` + exit 1 → escalate) runs after B' writes the plan and before upload. Rounds-2+ prompt now says **amend the existing plan**.
- **`agent-b.md`** — create (round 1) vs amend (rounds 2-6) mode keyed on `./plan.json` presence; formalized `dispositions`/`_amendments` emit schema; sticky-disposition rule.
- **`plan.round1.json`** stub fixture gains `dispositions` + empty `_amendments`.

## Tests
- `test_plan.py` (17 cases, RED before implementation): identical→OK, additions→OK, reworded reason same key→OK, dropped disposition/action unaccounted→flagged, drop recorded in `_amendments.removed`→OK, malformed/empty→no raise.
- Whole suite **132 passed**. YAML validated.
- Convergence itself is LLM-driven (not unit-testable) — verified by a live helm 3.21→4.2.1 re-run after merge (must converge instead of burning 6 rounds), per the spec.

## Scope
Only the 5 declared files; `b_round1`, all `c_round`s, `plan-approved`, `agent-d`, `escalate` untouched. Cold-reviewed (NO BLOCKERS); guard round-mapping (round2→plan-round1 … round6→plan-round5), step ordering, stub-mode triviality, and heredoc injection-safety all verified.

author: markdbodman
body:
## What

WSID Phase 3 — builds out two more profession corpora and introduces the **location (jurisdiction)** and **competency-level** variant model the goal called for, applicable across all coworker families.

Follows the merged data-architect corpus ([#1713](https://github.com/OpenDigitalProductFactory/opendigitalproductfactory/pull/1713)) and Phase 1 family profiles ([#1711](https://github.com/OpenDigitalProductFactory/opendigitalproductfactory/pull/1711)).

## Variant architecture (zero migration)

Design doc: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-13-wsid-location-competency-variants-design.md`.

- Two governed registries in `wiki-taxonomy.ts`: `PROFESSION_JURISDICTIONS` (`global|us|eu|uk`) and `PROFESSION_COMPETENCY_LEVELS` (`foundational|practitioner|expert`), each with a narrowing type guard.
- Two optional `WikiPageFrontmatter` fields: `professionJurisdiction[]`, `professionCompetencyLevel`. Validated fail-fast by the corpus seed; **not** DB columns in V1 (the gate-retrieval filter rides the future profile↔material binding). Omitted = `global` / `practitioner`, so the shipped data-architect corpus stays backward-compatible.
- `seedProfessionCorpus` tallies and the seed log surfaces per-family jurisdiction + competency coverage.

Rejected alternatives (documented in the spec): new typed columns (premature substrate, breaks the zero-migration design) and overloading `principleConsumerContexts` (diverges from the corpus pattern; `recallPrincipleContext` doesn't filter on it anyway).

## Content (distilled from FETCHED sources per the no-training-data rule)

**Software-engineer (9 pages, all open-license):** OWASP Top 10:2025 + ASVS, RFC 9110 HTTP semantics, SemVer, Conventional Commits, SLSA supply-chain levels, Google code-review standard.

**Finance (7 pages)** — proves the jurisdiction split: revenue recognition authored as separate, separately-cited **IFRS 15** (eu/uk) and **US-GAAP ASC 606** (us) pages; plus double-entry invariant, accrual basis, segregation of duties, the five internal-control components, and PCAOB audit standards (us). Sources: IFRS 15 official summary, GAO Green Book, PCAOB, Wikipedia (CC BY-SA).

Provenance discipline: FASB ASC full codification treated as licensed/checklist-only (conduit rule); SEC SOX pages that blocked the fetcher were **not** authored from un-fetched text — the unsourceable month-end-close and SOX-management pages were dropped rather than fabricated.

## Verification

Validated against the real seed-time logic (frontmatter parse + `extractPrinciplePayload` + variant guards) and esbuild syntax-checked all changed TS:

- **20 corpus pages, 0 orphan wiki-links**
- jurisdiction coverage: `global=17, us=2, eu=1, uk=1`
- competency coverage: `foundational=7, practitioner=9, expert=4`

author: alexander-turner
body:
## What & why

Follow-up to #620, which made ephemeral teardown run its `docker` commands in a
separate OS session so a spammed Ctrl-C can't cancel them and leak the throwaway
volumes. That PR shipped with invariant/unit tests (the helper creates a new
session; teardown routes every docker call through it) but **no end-to-end test
of the actual failure** — a real terminal Ctrl-C delivered to the launcher's
whole foreground process group.

This adds that e2e test. It launches the wrapper in its own session (so the test
signal can't escape to pytest), enters teardown, then delivers a real `SIGINT`
to the wrapper's process group during the first `volume rm`, and asserts every
throwaway volume is still removed with no survivor reported.

Two subtleties make it faithful — and are why a naive version would silently
pass against the bug:

- **A bash stub can't model docker.** Bash cannot un-ignore a signal that was
  `SIG_IGN` on entry, so a bash docker-stub keeps ignoring the inherited
  `trap '' INT` and survives *even un-detached*. Real docker (Go) re-installs
  its own handler via `sigaction`. The stub models this with a python child that
  resets `SIGINT` to default before signalling the group.
- The wrapper must be its own session/group leader (`start_new_session=True`) so
  `kill -INT -<pgid>` targets only the wrapper's group.

Verified the test **fails on the pre-#620 code** (config's `rm` is killed
mid-flight, volume leaks) and passes with the fix in place.

## Security boundary impact

None. Test-only; the boundary fix (the throwaway-volume guarantee holding under
Ctrl-C) already merged in #620. No SECURITY.md change.

## How it was tested

- `pytest tests/test_claude_wrapper.py -k "interrupt or teardown or ctrl_c"` — green.
- Confirmed fixed/unfixed discrimination by reverting the `cg_run_detached`
  wrapping in `ephemeral.bash`: the new test fails (config volume leaks); restored.
- [x] `pre-commit` hooks ran on commit (ruff/shellcheck/hygiene).

## Checklist

- [x] Commits use Conventional Commits (`<type>(<scope>): <desc>`)
- [x] Tests added/updated and not skipped or weakened
- [x] README/SECURITY.md touched only if a boundary change requires it (no change)
- [x] `[monitor-eval]` not added (monitor/eval harness unchanged)

## Lessons Learned

- **Testing signal delivery to a non-bash binary:** a bash stub cannot stand in
  for a program (docker, any Go/Rust CLI) when the test depends on that program
  receiving a signal the parent shell ignores. POSIX shells refuse to trap or
  reset a signal that was `SIG_IGN` on entry, so the stub silently inherits the
  ignore and survives — making the test pass regardless of the bug. Model the
  target with a process that calls `sigaction` directly (e.g. a small `python3`
  child doing `signal.signal(SIGINT, SIG_DFL)`) before asserting on signal
  delivery. **Where:** any test that fires a process-group signal at a CLI
  spawned under an interrupt-ignoring parent.

author: hanfour
body:
## 背景

(回應使用者選擇「完整接線到底」)在此之前 iOS 只在背景**單向推送**寵物到 iCloud、啟動時從不讀回,Mac 則完全不碰 iCloud — 兩端永遠無法顯示同一隻寵物。本 PR 在兩端接上完整的 read-merge-push 迴圈。

## 地基(純函式,完整單元測試)

- **`PetState.updatedAt`**:寫入時間戳(`PetStore.save` / `syncFullState` 設定)。additive + Codable 容錯;legacy JSON fallback 到 `lastInteraction`,避免遷移記錄被讀成 epoch。
- **`PetConflictResolver`**:單一寵物合併。
  - 同 `id` → 最新寫入勝(XP tiebreak)
  - 不同 `id`(首次同步碰撞)→ **投入較多者勝**(等級 → XP → 互動 → 較早出生 → 最新),避免某端剛生成的幼體蓋掉另一端養成的寵物
- **`PetSyncCoordinator`**:啟動時 `loadAndMigrate`(本地)+ 雲端合併、`push`(本地存檔 + syncFullState + KVS ping 喚醒他端)、live observe。可注入 `PetCloudSyncing` 協定供測試;無 iCloud 容器時優雅 no-op。

## 接線

- **iOS** `PeerDropApp`:啟動改用 `resolvedLaunchPet()`(合併)+ observe;背景 `push()` 取代 save-then-syncFullState。
- **Mac** `PeerDropMacApp` / `MacAppDelegate`:啟動合併 + observe;debounced 變更存檔、背景存檔、terminate 存檔全部 `push()` 到 iCloud(round 21 起原本只存本地)。
- **`PeerDrop-Mac.entitlements`**:iCloud 容器(`iCloud.com.hanfour.peerdrop`,與 iOS **同一個**)+ ubiquity-kvstore。

## ⚠️ Live iOS 行為改變

iOS 現在啟動時**會讀 iCloud 並合併**。resolver 採投入加權正是為了確保這不會回歸既有使用者的寵物。兩台原本各自獨立寵物的裝置會收斂到投入較多的那隻(單一寵物同步的本質,已於 runbook 記載)。

## 🙋 需要人工(只有你能做)

1. **Apple Developer portal**:`com.hanfour.peerdrop.mac` App ID 開 **iCloud**(Key-Value + iCloud Documents),綁定**既有**容器 `iCloud.com.hanfour.peerdrop`(勿建新的 `.mac` 容器)→ `get_provisioning_profile force:true` 重產 Mac profile。
2. **實機驗證**:Mac + iPhone 登入同一 iCloud 帳號,確認真的同步(我無法 runtime 驗證跨裝置 iCloud;模擬器也不可靠)。

詳見 `docs/release/release-runbook.md` 的 Mac iCloud 步驟。

## 測試

+9 `PetConflictResolver`、+8 `PetSyncCoordinator`(FakePetCloud 注入)。PeerDropKit **483/0**、iOS 測試 0 失敗、Mac build 綠(關簽章編譯檢查 — 已簽 Mac build 需 portal 能力)。

author: gasyoun
body:
## Why

Health check after merging #5–#10 surfaced two issues that the merge introduced.

## 1. The CI corpus job was dropped in the merge (regression)

#6 added a **Corpus integrity** job (schema validation + URN cross-check + artifact reproducibility). The dependabot action-version bumps (#2–#4) and #6 both edited `ci.yml`, and the merge **lost the corpus job** — the schema-validation guard that catches `vasilkov`/`poetics`-style drift was no longer in `main`.

Restored it (with `checkout@v6`/`setup-python@v6`) and **extended** it to cover every generator merged since — it now regenerates and diff-checks `tei/`, `pages/`, `visualizations.html`, `ramayana_epithets.json`, `nilakantha_profile.json`, `false_friends_profile.json` (was only the original five).

## 2. No `.gitattributes` (root cause of the CRLF churn)

`core.autocrlf=true` with no `.gitattributes` was behind every "LF will be replaced by CRLF" warning this session, and a real cross-platform risk for the CI reproducibility check. Added `* text=auto eol=lf` — renormalization was a **content no-op** (the index was already LF), so it just locks LF in and ends the churn.

## Also
- `requirements.txt` gains `indic-transliteration` (the `profile_nilakantha` dep the CI job needs).
- `ARCHITECTURE.md` scripts inventory synced to the merged whole (adds `build_visualizations`, `extract_false_friends_profile`, `profile_nilakantha`, `taxonomy`).

## Verified
- Merged `main` itself is healthy: validate ✓, URN cross-check ✓, all 8 artifacts regenerate **byte-identical** (the earlier "modified" status was pure line-ending noise).
- `ci.yml` valid YAML; the restored corpus job passes locally (`git diff --exit-code` = 0 after regenerating all six generators).

author: chasset
body:
## Quoi & pourquoi

**Premier palier du gros chantier** : l'outil déclaratif unifié des topologies ([ADR 0056](docs/decisions/0056-modele-declaratif-topologies.md)). Une topologie était définie **impérativement sur 6 lieux non synchronisés** (NODES en dur, inventaire, defaults, drapeaux WITH_CEPH/WITH_HARDENING, `-e`, prose). On les **unifie** : une topologie se **décrit** dans `topology.yaml`, l'outil en **dérive** les artefacts **sans état** (Ansible reste le moteur de convergence — ADR 0056 §7).

> Séquencement validé : **l'outil d'abord** (P0-P6), ha-3cp/#250 en sera le 1er vrai client (P7).

## Livré (P0 + moitié prod de P1)

- **`topology.example.yaml`** — schéma déclaratif générique : `catalog` (tuple ADR 0039), `nodes` (rôles cumulables → hyperconvergence), `network` (dont **`control_plane_lb`** = la VIP, dimension inexistante jusqu'ici), `exposition`, `storage`, `hardening`, `resources`, `target_kind`. **P0** : modéliser **révèle le delta ha-3cp**.
- **`cluster_topology/`** — modèle typé + **dérivations pures** (control/worker, garde-fou « > 1 CP ⇒ `control_plane_lb` requis », ADR 0047/0055) + générateur Jinja2.
- **🎯 INVARIANT P1 PROUVÉ** : `render_prod_inventory(topology.example.yaml)` == `bootstrap/hosts.example.yaml` **à l'octet** (commentaires inclus, via template versionné — éditer le template, pas le généré).
- **10 tests** (`test_cluster_topology.py`).
- **`jinja2`** ajouté aux deps (même moteur qu'Ansible — adoption ADR 0061) ; `topology.example.yaml` exclu de kubeconform (ce n'est pas un manifeste K8s — **2 listes synchronisées** package.json + lefthook).

## Garde-fou (ADR 0052)

Génération **read-only** → **aucun run banc requis** ; l'invariant est **prouvé par test**. Le garde-fou ha-3cp (preuve banc avant prod) ne s'applique pas (rien n'est déployé).

## Reste de P1 (PR suivantes)

Inventaire **banc** (`write_inventory`, format byte-exact cartographié) + group_vars → puis P2 (profil/défauts/graphe), P3 (CLI).

## Vérification

- [x] `pnpm lint` vert (ruff, yamllint, **110 tests**, jscpd, kubeconform avec exclusion) ; markdownlint OK ; pre-push hooks passent
- [x] Invariant byte-exact verrouillé par test ; `plan-modele-declaratif` Suivi à jour (P0 ✅, P1 🟡)

## Resumen
Dos mejoras del **simulacro**, independientes entre sí y del resto de modos:

### 1. Editar preguntas en el simulacro
- Botón ✏️ en la vista de pregunta del simulacro (`EXAM._isSim`), con el mismo aspecto y posición que en el modo estudio, reutilizando `openEditModal` sin duplicar lógica.
- Nuevo helper `editContext(idx)`: resuelve la fuente real de la pregunta (`EXAM.questions` con `_group`/`_temaId` en simulacro/cajón vs `state` en estudio), de modo que la clave `fusion_edit_*` y el índice `fusion_editindex_*` usan **el tema de origen correcto**.
- Al guardar/quitar la edición se refresca en memoria el array activo y se invalida `dataCache` del tema, propagando el override a **todos los modos** (estudio, examen, puntos débiles, favoritas, simulacro, cajón). Re-render con `renderExamQuestion` **sin perder** temporizador, posición ni respuesta pendiente.

### 2. Descarte de preguntas dominadas
- Registro `fusion_sim_mastery` → `{ [group_temaId_qn]: { group, temaId, qn, aciertos } }`.
- En `finishExam` (solo `_isSim`): acierto → `aciertos+1`, fallo → reset a `0`. Umbral **3 aciertos seguidos** = dominada.
- `launchSim` **excluye las dominadas antes** de la anti-repetición (`fusion_sim_seen_*`); si no queda ninguna, muestra toast y no lanza. `pick = min(nQuestions, pool)` absorbe el caso de pool insuficiente.
- Indicador en el configurador del simulacro: `🏆 N preguntas dominadas (no aparecerán)`.

## Lo que NO se toca
- El cajón de errores (`fusion_cajon`, `_isCajon`) sigue independiente.
- Los demás modos de examen (⏱ 🎯 ❤️ 🔁) no se ven afectados.
- `finishExam()` solo añade el bloque de mastery dentro de `_isSim`.

author: hellblazer
body:
## Summary

Fixes the flaky `CrossProcessMigration2PCInstrumentationTest.abortedMigrationWritesPrepareThenAbortToWal` that went **RED on a main CI run** (post-merge of #248, unrelated to that PR's code).

**Root cause** (verified by reading `CrossProcessMigration`): the test built the 2PC orchestrator with `MigrationConfig.defaults()` (100ms phase / 300ms total timeout) but never called `setClock()`, so it ran on the real system clock (`Clock.system()`). Each WAL append fsyncs (`force(true)`); under CI load the PREPARE fsync + work blows the budget, firing a timeout branch (`PREPARE_TIMEOUT` / `ABORT_TIMEOUT`) that completes the migration future **without** writing ABORT to the WAL → a PREPARE-only (incomplete) log → `assertTrue(incomplete.isEmpty())` fails.

The production skip-ABORT-on-timeout is **defensible** (don't mark a transaction resolved when rollback didn't complete — recovery rolls it back), so this is a **test-determinism** defect, fixed per the TEST_FRAMEWORK_GUIDE Clock-injection procedure.

## Changes (test-only)

- Inject a **constant clock** (`TickingClock` delta-per-read 0) into the two WAL tests (success + abort) so the wall-clock timeout guards can never spuriously fire and the clean `PREPARE→COMMIT` / `PREPARE→ABORT` paths are taken deterministically.
- Add `timedOutMigrationLeavesPrepareIncompleteForRecovery`: a **fast clock** (delta 500ms) forces a timeout and asserts the migration fails leaving the PREPARE incomplete for recovery — pinning the production contract and proving the root cause. (Non-vacuous: `assertFalse(incomplete.isEmpty())` precedes the `allMatch(PREPARE)` check.)

## Verification

- 6/6 (2 fixed + 1 new + 3 existing) green, stable across 3 repeated local runs.
- Stacked review (code-review-expert + substantive-critic), round-2 clean: **0 Critical / 0 Significant**. Round-1 caught a misleading comment in the new test (the fast clock trips `PREPARE_TIMEOUT` first, so `commit/abort` are never entered) — corrected, and the `Dest` flag clarified as never-consulted.

## Residual gap (tracked, not in scope)

Both reviewers flagged a real production durability gap: the timeout / rollback-failure paths write **no ABORT tombstone**, so recovery cannot distinguish a timed-out-mid-rollback from a clean-rollback-then-crash, and source re-add idempotency is unverified. Filed as **Luciferase-9kjpt (P2)**.

body:
## Summary
- split the package manifest schema from the internal runtime model
- introduce `PackageDefinition` and move runtime package matching logic to it
- keep `PackageManifest` focused on manifest file deserialization and validation
- convert registry, engine, DB, and command flows to use `PackageDefinition`
- rename call sites and fields to reflect the new boundary (`manifest` -> `pkg` / `definition` where appropriate)

## Intent
`PackageManifest` had been used both as the external manifest-file format and as the internal package model.
This change separates those concerns so that:
- manifest parsing/validation stays at the file boundary
- internal flows work with a model that owns `PackageId`
- runtime and persistence code no longer depend directly on the manifest schema

This also removes repeated `PackageId` reconstruction from manifest values and makes the package/runtime terminology more explicit across the codebase.

## Compatibility notes
- local DB persistence is intentionally not backward-compatible with the previous shape
- this is acceptable because the software has not been released yet
- no user-facing manifest format change is intended in this PR; the refactor is internal to how manifests are represented after loading

- `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`

1. **`convenience`가 잡동사니 서랍** — 붙여넣기·컨트롤 바·Dock·알림·스크롤바·워크스페이스 선택기·리소스 수명주기 등 무관한 18개 필드가 한 객체/섹션에 뒤섞임.
2. **최상위 키 난립** — `appThemeId`, `appFont`, `workspaceDisplay`, `workspaceSortOrder` 등 laymux 고유 설정이 일관성 없이 흩어짐.

이 PR은 settings.json 스키마와 Settings UI를 **도메인별 응집 그룹**으로 재분류한다.

## 스키마 변경 (settings.json, camelCase)

WT 호환 코어(`profiles`/`colorSchemes`/`keybindings`/`profileDefaults`/`defaultProfile`)와 구조 상태(`workspaces`/`layouts`/`docks`)는 최상위 유지.

| 새 그룹 | 흡수한 (구→신) |
|---|---|
| `appearance` | appThemeId→themeId, appFont→font |
| `paste` | smartPaste→smart, pasteImageDir→imageDir, smartRemoveIndent→removeIndent, smartRemoveLineBreak→removeLineBreak, smartLinkJoin→linkJoin, largePasteWarning→largeWarning, pastePathSeparator→pathSeparator, pastePathQuote→pathQuote |
| `terminal` (확장) | copyOnSelect, scrollbarStyle (+ 기존 outputActivityBurst) |
| `controlBar` | hoverIdleSeconds, defaultControlBarMode→defaultMode |
| `dock` | dockPersistState→persistState, dockArrowNav→arrowNav, dockArrowFocusPane→arrowFocusPane |
| `notifications` | notificationDismiss→dismiss |
| `workspaceSelector` | workspaceDisplay→display, workspaceSortOrder→sortOrder, pathEllipsis, hiddenAutoCloseSeconds |

제거된 최상위 키: `convenience`, `appThemeId`, `appFont`, `workspaceDisplay`, `workspaceSortOrder`, 레거시 `font`.

> ⚠️ **의도된 breaking change**: 내부 개발 단계라 마이그레이션 코드는 두지 않는다(no-backward-compat 정책). 구 키는 무시되고 이동된 필드는 기본값으로 리셋된다. 이는 의도된 동작이다.

## Settings UI

평평한 사이드바를 그룹 헤더(**Appearance / Terminal / Interface / Integrations / Views / Input / Profiles**)로 묶고, Convenience 섹션을 **Paste · Terminal · Interface**(Control Bar·Dock·Notifications 하위 카드)로 분해. path-ellipsis·hidden-auto-close는 Workspaces로 이동.

## 부수 효과 (latent bug fix)

Rust `ConvenienceSettings`에 없어 매 저장마다 리셋되던 4개 필드(`hoverIdleSeconds`, `defaultControlBarMode`, `notificationDismiss`, `dockArrowFocusPane`)가, 신 Rust 구조체가 영속 필드를 완전히 미러링하면서 자동 해소됨.

## 검증

- Rust: `cargo test settings`(65 passed) / `clippy` / `fmt` ✓
- TS: `tsc` 0 errors / `vitest` 2115 passed / `eslint` 0 errors / `prettier` / `vite build` ✓
- dev(19281) 실측: 신 사이드바 그룹·분리 섹션 렌더 + settings.json 신 스키마 저장 라운드트립 확인

## What

Adds the ability to edit an existing mortgage transaction from the mortgage page. Previously the UI only supported adding and deleting transactions, even though the backend already exposed `PATCH /api/mortgages/transactions/:id` (which reconciles the mortgage's outstanding balance by reversing the old transaction's effect and applying the edited one inside a `db.transaction`).

## Changes

- **New hook** `useUpdateMortgageTransaction` — issues the `PATCH`, normalizes the response, and invalidates the `['mortgages']` and `['dashboard']` query keys (mirrors the create/delete hooks).
- **`MortgageTxnHistory`** — adds a per-row edit (pencil) button and an `onEdit` callback, mirroring `PropertyTxnHistory` in the investments feature.

When editing a repayment, the live-preview balance adds back the old transaction's principal so the projected balance stays accurate. The modal title and confirm label switch to "Edit Transaction" / "Save Changes".

## Why

Brings the mortgage transaction history to parity with the investments-property transaction history, which already supported inline editing. Without this, correcting a mistyped repayment/valuation/rate-change required deleting and re-adding the transaction.

author: graemef
body:
The Tier-3 residue of the hexagonal test-architecture epic (comms-e5vm): the **one** assertion in the suite that genuinely cannot leave the socket — that interrupting an in-flight \`FetchHttpClient\` long-poll on scope close actually tears down the underlying TCP connection (\`AbortSignal → fetch → socket\`).

## Why this is the only surviving socket test

comms-e5vm.2 (#12) moved every event-pump **LOGIC** test — gap-replay, 429 retry, BAD_EVENT_QUEUE_ID reconnect, and the Effect **fiber-interrupt** path of scope close — onto the owned-fake stub HttpClient + TestClock: deterministic, no socket. The stub proves the *fiber* unwinds. It cannot prove the *socket* unwinds, because there is no socket. This test closes exactly that gap and is the only surviving \`Bun.serve\` long-poll in the suite.

## The assertion is server-side

A real \`Bun.serve\` whose long-poll handler parks forever but listens on the request's \`req.signal\`. When the client tears the connection down, Bun fires that abort — observing it is proof the teardown reached the peer, not merely that our Effect fiber unwound (which the stub already covers). The Effect platform client wires this end to end: \`httpClient.make\` aborts the request's \`AbortController\` \`onInterrupt\`, and \`FetchHttpClient\` passes that \`signal\` into \`fetch\`.

Lifecycle is \`Effect.acquireRelease\`/\`Scope\` throughout: the server's release is \`server.stop(true)\`, and the long-poll is forked into an inner \`Effect.scoped\` whose close is the interruption under test — so release is guaranteed even on the interruption path. The proof is timeout-guarded, so a non-teardown fails loud (verified by a mutation: detaching the fiber from the scope makes the test time out).

## Broader-rework question (comms-4lz5's original scope): recommend **leave-as-is**

The bead also asked whether to migrate the ~170 \`realm.\`/\`fixture.\` hook call sites to a per-test \`Effect.scoped\` wrapper. That rework was motivated by a contention-driven teardown-starvation flake in the infinite-long-poll tests — which .2 dissolved structurally by moving that logic off the socket. Every fixture still wired through \`registerRealmHooks\` is now a plain request/response realm that starts and stops in a few ms; there is no teardown-starvation mode left to fix, and the \`acquireRelease\`/\`Scope\` shape now lives exactly where it is load-bearing (this one socket test). The migration would be churn across ~170 sites for no behavioural payoff — YAGNI. This PR also refreshes the now-stale \`realm-hooks.ts\` doc comment that still described the dissolved failure mode.

Closes comms-4lz5.

author: simonkirkham
body:
## What
Retry transient DynamoDB timeouts inside the projection rebuild's **reads**, and map a persistent timeout to **503** instead of an unhandled **500**.

## Why
BUG-23: `POST /admin/projections/rebuild` returned an unhandled 500 on a transient `TimeoutException` (AWSSDK.Core, prod 2026-06-05). The rebuild's writes already retried via `BoundedWrites`; the reads (`ReadAllStreamsAsync` + the 8 reconcile `QueryAll`/`GetAll` scans) did not — one transient blip aborted the whole rebuild, and `LoggingConfig.Map` had no arm for `TimeoutException` so it fell to 500.

## Changes
| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `BoundedWrites.cs` | Add result-returning `WithRetryAsync<T>` overload (void overload delegates to it); reads share the same bounded backoff. `IsTransient` already covered `TimeoutException` + non-caller `OperationCanceledException`. |
| `ProjectionRebuildHandler.cs` | Wrap `ReadAllStreamsAsync` and every reconcile read in `BoundedWrites.WithRetryAsync`. |
| `LoggingConfig.cs` | `Map`: persistent `TimeoutException` → 503 "timed out, retry"; `OperationCanceledException` → 503 only when the request was **not** client-aborted (genuine aborts still 500). 503 logs at **Warning** (transient, recoverable), not Error. |
| `AdminHandlers.cs` | Comment: `ProjectionRebuildFault` now only fires on a genuinely-unfinishable rebuild (a recovered transient never reaches the catch). |

## Tests
`tests/Api.Integration/RebuildTimeoutTests.cs` (4, HTTP-level via WebApplicationFactory):
- transient `TimeoutException` on a rebuild read → 200 (retry recovered)
- persistent `TimeoutException` → 503, not 500
- transient/persistent `OperationCanceledException` with a foreign token (SDK per-op timeout) → 200 / 503

Written failing first against current 500 behaviour. Green: `dotnet build`, Api.Integration (382), Domain.Specs (195), `cdk synth`.

## Deploy-time impact
Neutral. No infra/CI/CDK change (`cdk synth` unchanged). Pure handler/middleware logic.

author: colonelpanic8
body:
## Why

The whiff / beaten-to-ball detector (`src/stats/calculators/whiff.rs`) was precision-tuned with strict arming gates, so it misses many genuine attempts at the ball. We're repurposing it as the front end of a human **confirm/reject review loop** in rocket-sense (`event_reviews`) whose goal is to build a *labeled dataset* of whiffs / beaten-to-ball / attempts. For that job the detector should err toward **recall**: flag essentially any committed move at a nearby ball that did not produce a touch as a *candidate*, and let reviewers prune the false positives. Precision is recovered downstream from the labels, not in the detector.

## What

Loosen the **non-dodge approach path** and the **shared distance/time gates**:

| constant | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `WHIFF_ENTER_DISTANCE` | 150 | 220 |
| `WHIFF_EXIT_DISTANCE` | 285 | 360 |
| `WHIFF_MAX_CANDIDATE_SECONDS` | 0.65 | 1.0 |
| `WHIFF_MIN_APPROACH_SPEED` | 700 | 350 |
| `WHIFF_MIN_CLOSING_SPEED` | 450 | 250 |
| `WHIFF_MIN_FORWARD_ALIGNMENT` | 0.55 | 0.3 |
| `WHIFF_MIN_VELOCITY_ALIGNMENT` | 0.7 | 0.45 |
| `WHIFF_MAX_LATERAL_OFFSET` | 120 | 200 |

The **dodge-specific gates are left stricter** so a clear side-dodge past the ball is still not treated as an attempt (keeps an anchor negative).

No `WhiffEvent` / `WhiffEventKind` schema change, so **TS bindings are unaffected** and propagation to rocket-sense stays a pure `sync-subtr-actor`.

## Tests

- All existing whiff tests pass, including the "not an attempt" negatives (lateral drive-by, velocity-matched pacing, side dodge) kept as anchors.
- Added `loosened_detector_counts_moderate_speed_approach_as_candidate` covering a ~500 uu/s approach that was below the old 700 gate and now registers as a candidate.

## Follow-up (not in this PR)

This is phase 1. Next: `sync-subtr-actor` into rocket-sense so these candidates flow into the existing `event_reviews` confirm/reject system, then deploy. The collected labels become regression test cases for the detector.

body:
Closes #31.

## Problem

On a site running `sigx`/`@sigx/server-renderer` 0.6.x + `@sigx/ssg` 0.11.0, `LivePreview` islands fail after a client-side (SPA) navigation, logging `[live-code] No props found for LivePreview island` and never hydrating the preview. Hard load is clean; only arriving via SPA navigation breaks.

## Root cause

The issue's hypothesis (live-code depending on the removed `serializeProps` / `window.__SIGX_STATE__`) is a red herring — live-code never used those. `data-island-props` is a plain HTML attribute baked into the compiled MDX vnodes by the SSG shiki transformer.

Under core 0.6 an MDX page's island markup compiles to **keyless** vnodes, so on SPA navigation the framework's reconciler **reuses** a previous route's `.live-preview-island` `<div>` and patches its attributes *in place* rather than replacing the node. Because live-code renders out-of-band (`island.innerHTML = ''` + its own `render()` root), it fights that reconciliation, and at the instant live-code re-scans, the reused island's `data-island-props` is transiently absent (or not yet rewritten to the new route's value). The old code treated that as a hard error and gave up.

## Fix (self-contained in the client; no consumer change)

- Treat a missing `data-island-props` as an **expected transient** during SPA churn: skip silently and leave the island unhydrated so a later pass retries, instead of logging an error.
- **Observe `data-island-props` attribute mutations** on the island subtree. When the framework writes the destination route's props onto a reused island, live-code re-syncs (tearing down the now-stale out-of-band preview via the existing cleanup path) and hydrates with the new props. `childList` mutations alone miss in-place attribute rewrites on reused nodes.

This complements the SPA stale-preview cleanup shipped in #20/#19 and keeps the no-consumer-change approach that PR established.

## Tests

Adds the repo's first vitest suite (happy-dom) reproducing the SPA-navigation hydration race:

- island present on hard load hydrates;
- transiently-missing props no longer error and stay retryable, then hydrate once the attribute appears;
- a reused island whose props are rewritten in place re-hydrates with the new props.

Verified the two SPA-navigation tests **fail** against the un-fixed `client.tsx` and pass with the fix. Test files are excluded from the declaration build and the published tarball; added a minimal root `vitest.config.ts` (sigx JSX transform + test glob).

## Verification

`pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm test` (3 passing), `pnpm build`, and `pnpm size` (45.56 kB ≤ 200 kB) all pass.

## Docs

No public API change. The SignalX docs site (signalxjs/signalxjs.github.io#131 / #40) will bump `@sigx/live-code` once this ships, per the refresh playbook.

body:
## Summary

Extracts the ~150 lines of duplicated LSCM least-squares system-assembly logic shared between `AngleBasedLSCM::ComputeImpl` and `HierarchicalLSCM::solveLSCMLevel` into a new `detail::lscm::buildSystem` utility (`include/OpenABF/detail/LSCMSystem.hpp`). Both call sites now delegate pin placement + matrix assembly to the new utility and keep only their solver-specific bits (warm-start, solver dispatch, UV write-back).

Also closes the existing `freeIdxTable` container drift (`std::map` in ABLSCM, `std::unordered_map` in HLSCM) by unifying on `std::unordered_map`. Numerically inert — both call sites use `.at()` lookup only.

Closes #64. Unblocks P6 (re-evaluate scope now that the face-assembly loop lives in `buildSystem`).

## Changes

### Core refactor
- **New header** `include/OpenABF/detail/LSCMSystem.hpp` — the extracted utility with `SystemParts<T>` and `buildSystem<T, MeshType>()`.
- **`AngleBasedLSCM::ComputeImpl`** — replaced ~127 lines of inline assembly with a `buildSystem` call. Dead `<cmath>` and `<map>` includes dropped.
- **`HierarchicalLSCM::solveLSCMLevel`** — replaced ~112 lines with a `buildSystem` call.

### Build / packaging
- **`CMakeLists.txt`** — added `install(DIRECTORY)` rule for `include/OpenABF/detail/` so multiheader installs ship the new header (the existing `PUBLIC_HEADER` rule flattens).
- **`single_include/OpenABF/OpenABF.hpp`** — regenerated via `thirdparty/amalgamate`. No `single_include.json` edit needed.

### Tests
- New `LSCMSystemBuild` gtest fixture in `tests/src/TestParameterization.cpp` with four direct tests:
  - `Dimensions_KnownMesh` — A is `2·numFaces × 2·numFree`, b is `2·numFaces × 1`
  - `FreeIdxTable_Population` — size, pin exclusion, contiguous slots
  - `PinRowsLandInB` — walks A's iterator and asserts no column exceeds the free-vertex range
  - `FreeIdxTable_DeterministicAcrossRuns` — 4×4 grid, 14 free verts, asserts slot assignment is run-invariant

### Docs (bonus — addresses pre-existing A9 issue)
- Removed all 11 `@internal` tags across `HierarchicalLSCM.hpp` and `detail/LSCMSystem.hpp`. A9 had added them to `detail::hlscm::{Quadric, CollapseRecord, HierarchyLevel, DecimationMesh}` and to four free functions. With Doxygen's default `INTERNAL_DOCS = NO`, the tagged doc blocks were silently dropped, after which Doxygen flagged the now-undocumented compounds as warnings. Since OpenABF ships as headers, the `detail::` namespace name carries the "don't depend on this" signal regardless of doc tags. Removing the tags is simpler than configuring around them and gets the same end state (compounds render with their authored docs). **Eliminates 5 Doxygen warnings.**

## Numerical correctness

Existing parameterization regression tests use `EXPECT_FLOAT_EQ` / `EXPECT_DOUBLE_EQ` against hardcoded baseline UVs and pass unchanged → bit-identical results within 4 ULP for both call sites, including the multi-level HLSCM path (`HLSCM.MultiLevelHierarchy`, `HLSCM.ABFPlusPlusAnglePreservation` on a curved hemisphere, `HLSCMInternal.SolveLSCMLevel_KnownMesh`).

## Test plan

- [x] New `LSCMSystemBuild` direct tests pass (4/4)
- [x] Full ctest suite passes (6/6) on multiheader build
- [x] Single-header build of `OpenABF_TestParameterization` passes
- [x] Multiheader install + downstream consumer build + run verified locally
- [x] Single-header install + downstream consumer build + run verified locally
- [x] Doxygen build clean of all A8/A9-related warnings (63 → 58 total; the 5 cleared are the `@internal` compound warnings)
- [x] `git clang-format` clean
- [x] Amalgam regenerated and committed

CI exercises multiheader=ON and multiheader=OFF install paths across 4 distros (`.github/workflows/install.yml`) plus build/test combinations (`.gitlab-ci.yml`).

- **« Toute la courbe ne rentre pas dans le graphe »** : suppression du cadrage `keepRiseFocus` + du `clipT` dans `SvgBACForecast` → la courbe projetée va jusqu'à son retour à 0 ; garde-fou `truncated` avec marqueur explicite si l'horizon est atteint.
- **Unités/format** : formateur de durée unique `fmtDurationHM` ; ABV affiché en `%` (et non `°`) dans la liste de la carte ; labels d'axe X des deux charts BAC ancrés aux bords (plus de débordement).

## Onglet Stats — nouveaux contenus & revue des calculs

- Section **« Calendrier »** : heatmap des grammes d'alcool par jour (`SvgCalendarHeatmap`, intensité par bandes).
- Section **« Sessions »** : liste des dernières sessions (date, durée, nb de verres, pic coloré) + histogramme de la distribution des pics.
- Card **« Cumul vs période précédente »** dans Évolution (`SvgLineChart` généralisé avec `singleAxis`).
- Agrégations inline **extraites en helpers purs testables** : `computeMonthlyTrends`, `computeRollingDaily`, `computeSessionDurationBuckets`, `buildHeatmapCells`, `buildSessionList`, `buildSessionPeakHistogram`, `buildCumulativeComparison`.

## Onglet Catégories — couleur

Slider de teinte (0-359) + bouton **« Auto »** dans `EditCategorySheet`. Persistance setting `cat.color.id.<id>` (miroir des icônes, **rename-safe**) ; `applyCatHueOverrides` applique la teinte au registre `CAT` (clone des défauts pour ne jamais corrompre `CAT_DEFAULT`), via `CategoryColorsContext` + seed boot (pas de flash). Aperçu live de la pastille/icône.

## Général — roue horaire iOS

`WheelPicker` / `TimeWheelSheet` / `TimeField` (scroll-snap natif + tap-to-select + clavier) remplacent `<input type="time">` dans l'ajout et l'édition d'entrée. La date reste un input natif.

## Tests & build

- **165 tests** verts (`npm test`), dont ~32 nouveaux : moteur de prévision (continuité t=0, montée d'absorption, fin à 0), fenêtre 48 h, `bucketSpend` 4 granularités, tendances/moyennes mobiles, heatmap/sessions/cumul, `applyCatHueOverrides`, maths de la roue, end-to-end couleur (slider clavier → setting → carte) et roue horaire (tap → DB).

## Tests manuels conseillés

- BAC : ajouter une bière maintenant → la prévision monte d'abord puis redescend, toute la courbe visible ; « Sobriété/Conduite » montrent l'heure cible.
- Catégorie : Modifier → slider Teinte → la pastille se recolore ; « Auto » revient au défaut ; persiste au reload + après renommage.

author: rudrakhp
body:
**Please provide a description of this PR:**
- Adds support for excluding namespaces and hosts from a Sidecar egress listener's hosts, using a `~` prefix on the namespace. Chose this prefix since `~/*` is already supported today and this logically extends the same convention.
- Semantics:
  - `~ns/*` exclude every host in namespace `ns`.
  - `~ns/host` exclude `host` within `ns`.
  - `~/host`exclude `host` across all namespaces (`~` alone maps to the wildcard namespace).
  - `~/*` import nothing, already supported.
- Exclusion is applied over inclusion: a host is selected if `included && !excluded`. Affects both `selectServices` (clusters) and `SelectVirtualServices` (routes).
- For multi-host VirtualServices, a host excluded on one entry doesn't drop the VS if another host still qualifies, the VS is removed only when all matching hosts are excluded.
- Validation changes to support the new semantics.

Related #60139

author: evgenyandroid
body:
## Why
The daily watcher reported `spec_release.latest_tag: v3.0.15` while the spec line had advanced to **3.1.0-rc.14**. Root cause is one line: it fetched `GET /releases/latest`, and **GitHub's `/releases/latest` deliberately excludes prereleases**. Every RC is a prerelease, so the watcher was structurally blind to the entire `3.1.0-rc.*` line — rc.10→rc.14 all published with zero notifications, and were spotted on the releases page first.

## Fix
Keep `/releases/latest` for the stable tag, and add a second probe via `/releases` (which **does** include prereleases, newest-first) to record `latest_prerelease_tag` when it differs. Now each new RC diffs as a state change and fires the watcher email.

```
latest_tag:            v3.0.15        # stable, meaning unchanged
latest_prerelease_tag: v3.1.0-rc.14   # NEW — RC line, previously invisible
```

## Verification
- `node --check` passes.
- Simulated the new block against the live GitHub API → output above (exact).
- Additive only; `latest_tag` retains its stable-only semantics for existing callers.

**Part of #314** (the methylation panel's ~28-row unrelated-PMID epic). This lands the **glutathione / antioxidant pathway-group** slice — 4 rows, none of which has an open per-row issue — replacing each row's off-topic citations with gene/variant-specific references. **Every title was verified via NCBI esummary and the functional direction with the Consensus connector.** #314 stays open as the epic tracker.

| Row | Was (off-topic) | Now (verified) |
|-----|-----------------|----------------|
| **SOD2** rs4880 Val16Ala | 10085127 (cerebral-ischemia NOS-2), 15509580 (celastrols/heat-shock) | 12618592 + 15864132 (Sutton 2003/2005, MnSOD Ala16Val mitochondrial import — functional), 23952573 (Bresciani 2013 review) |
| **GPX1** rs1050450 Pro198Leu | 15504747 (sphingosine-1-phosphate), 17709398 (Swi/Snf histone) | 16287877 (Ravn-Haren 2006, activity/breast), 19415410 (Jabłońska 2009, activity/selenium), 35626163 (Zhao 2022 review) |

author: josephcarey
body:
Implements the backend-hardening batch from the v1 codebase audit (`docs/reviews/v1-audit.md`). Scope limited to `src/api/**`, `src/lib/read-api/**`, `src/lib/db/**` (+ the `D1_MAX_BATCH` move). `bun run ci` is green (868 tests).

## Findings addressed

- **§6.1 [High] Public rate-limiter bypass** — `clientKey` bucketed by the raw, unvalidated bearer token, so a fresh random `Bearer <junk>` per request earned a new bucket every time and evaded the per-IP budget. Now resolves the token first and only keys `token:<id>` when it passes the same validity check as viewer resolution (active token whose snapshot owner still matches the agent); otherwise keys by IP. Regression tests cover random-token spray, valid-token bucketing, and stale owner-mismatched tokens falling back to IP.
- **§6.3 [Low] `touchLastUsed` could 500 a valid auth** — the advisory `last_used_at` write was awaited outside any try/catch. Wrapped so it logs and continues, never gating auth; added a test injecting a failing touch write.
- **§2.1 [Medium] Leaderboard omitted the symbol** — added `agent_symbol` to the public `LeaderboardRow` (resolved via `getSymbolsByIds`) and the OpenAPI schema. Additive/backwards-compatible; `agent_id` retained.
- **§7.4 [Medium] Adapter `batch()` non-atomic** — the shared in-memory D1 adapter ran statements sequentially with no transaction, so the atomicity `applyRatingPeriod`/season-close rely on was untested. Wrapped `batch()` in a `SAVEPOINT` with best-effort rollback on any statement failure; added a partial-failure rollback test. Also standardised the `bot-auth` suite onto the shared adapter (§7.4b).
- **§7.2 [Medium] `unrankedUntilFor` boundaries** — added `close.test.ts` with gap=0, negative gap, year-wrap, leap-day (2028), non-leap Feb, and time-component cases.
- **§1.4 [Nit] `D1_MAX_BATCH` coupling** — moved from `snapshots.ts` to `src/lib/db/constants.ts` and updated all importers (`ratings`, `rounds`, `snapshots`, `import-pipeline`). The audit said "two importers"; there were more, all updated to keep the build green.

## Misdiagnosis noted

- **§7.3 [Low] Batch-overflow throw untested** — this is **already** covered in `src/lib/db/ratings.test.ts` ("throws (fail-loud)… too large for a single atomic batch"), which asserts both the descriptive message and that nothing (not even the marker) was applied. No duplicate test added.

## Review note
A rubber-duck pass tightened two things post-implementation: the limiter now uses the full owner-match validity predicate (not just "active token"), and the savepoint cleanup is best-effort so a conflict-mode abort can't mask the original error.

Do not merge — opened for review.

🔗 **View agent run:** https://app.netlify.com/projects/ghar-ka-zaiqa/agent-runs/6a2d315f782e63a6f3404754

🤖 **Agent:** Claude

💬 **Prompt:** I published my project but it is showing page not found

✅ **Result:** The site was showing "page not found" because Netlify had no configuration file telling it where the HTML files live. Without a `netlify.toml`, Netlify defaults to publishing from the repository root, but this project's `index.html` and all frontend assets reside in the `frontend/` subdirectory.

A `netlify.toml` was created at the repository root with the publish directory set to `frontend`. This tells Netlify to serve the site from the correct folder, resolving the 404 error. No other changes were needed — the backend API is already configured to point at an external host (`https://wms-pk.solaxpower.com/lunchbox-api`) for production, so it will continue to work as before.

author: sugumaran-balasubramaniyan
body:
## Summary

Two related bugs where named custom providers (`custom:<name>`) were not correctly resolved in the auxiliary client and vision routing, causing HTTP 400 errors and silent fallback to wrong endpoints.

### Root Cause 1 — `_normalize_aux_provider` in `agent/auxiliary_client.py`

After stripping the `custom:` prefix (e.g., `custom:kimi` → `kimi`), the function continued to apply `_PROVIDER_ALIASES` rewriting. This meant `custom:kimi` became `kimi-coding` (a built-in), routing auxiliary calls to Kimi's built-in endpoint instead of the user's named custom provider. Similarly `custom:glm` became `zai`.

### Root Cause 2 — `_supports_vision_override` in `agent/image_routing.py`

The vision capability lookup iterated only over the literal `provider` and `config_provider` strings when keying into the `providers:` dict. Config dict keys never include the `custom:` prefix, so `custom:openclaw-router` failed to match the dict key `openclaw-router`.

## Fix

1. **`agent/auxiliary_client.py`**: When the input starts with `custom:`, return the suffix immediately without applying `_PROVIDER_ALIASES`. The `custom:` prefix is the user's explicit signal that they reference their own named provider.

2. **`agent/image_routing.py`**: The providers dict candidate-key loop now also tries each candidate with the `custom:` prefix stripped.

## Changes

| File | Change | Lines |
|------|--------|-------|
| `agent/auxiliary_client.py` | Return custom: suffix without alias rewriting | +8 / -1 |
| `agent/image_routing.py` | Try stripped custom: prefix as dict key | +7 / -1 |

Closes #45472, closes #45480

author: joeeblack
body:
* 🚨 Severity: CRITICAL
* 💡 Vulnerability: Command injection vulnerability in `SettingsView.swift` when constructing AppleScript `do shell script` commands containing dynamic properties like the application bundle path. If a user renames the app or places it in a path with bash control characters like `; rm -rf /`, it would be executed as root since it uses "with administrator privileges".
* 🎯 Impact: Arbitrary code execution as root if the bundle path or uninstaller script path contains malicious characters.
* 🔧 Fix: Secured string interpolation by applying double escaping:
  1. Bash escaping: Wrapping the path and arguments in single quotes and replacing inner single quotes.
  2. AppleScript string literal escaping: Replacing backslashes and double quotes in the generated command string.
* ✅ Verification: Verified the code compiles and correctly escapes strings according to the `do shell script` security requirements. Code review passed.

body:
Add Ripple, Sparkle, Volume Ring, and Audio Ripple modes

Non-audio mode 3 - Ripple: color pulses outward from center hex to the outer
ring in 3 steps (center lit, ring lit, all off) then cycles to the next palette
color; left pot controls step speed (100–800 ms per step)

Non-audio mode 4 - Sparkle: random LEDs across all panels light in random
palette colors and fade at 0.8x per frame; maintains its own pixel buffer so
the per-frame strip.clear() does not erase the fade trail; left pot controls
spark density (1–20 new sparks per frame)

Audio mode 3 - Volume Ring: total audio energy (average of all three bands)
drives how many hex panels light up, filling outward from center like a VU
meter; left pot selects color

Audio mode 4 - Audio Ripple: a bass spike triggers a 3-step ripple (center →
ring → dim ring) advancing every 150 ms; only fires when idle so beats do not
interrupt mid-ripple; left pot selects color

Also bumped NUM_AUDIO_MODES and NUM_NON_AUDIO_MODES from 3 to 5.

author: chrisrackauckas-claude
body:
## Problem

The Core test leg was fixed in #61 by passing `apt-packages: "python3-scipy"` to the `grouped-tests.yml@v1` caller in `CI.yml`. However, the **Downgrade** leg still fails with `No module named scipy` because `Downgrade.yml` never provisioned scipy onto the runner's system python3.

PyCall builds against the runner's system python3; `using SciPyDiffEq` then resolves scipy via `pyimport_conda`, which falls back to a plain `pyimport` here (PyCall is not Conda-managed). Without scipy installed into that system python, the import fails.

## Fix

As of SciML/.github **v1.13**, the reusable `downgrade.yml@v1` workflow supports an `apt-packages` input. This PR passes `apt-packages: "python3-scipy"` to the Downgrade caller, mirroring what #61 did for the Core/grouped-tests leg.

Only the workflow config file (`.github/workflows/Downgrade.yml`) is touched; no test logic changed. `actionlint` is clean.

Ignore until reviewed by @ChrisRackauckas.

author: dcadenas
body:
Opening a large opening-repertoire PGN froze the move-notation panel for ~9s. The trigger was a multi-game repertoire merged into one deeply nested variation tree — thousands of half-move nodes and many inline comments. Each move cell renders eagerly with several store subscriptions, so the whole WebView blocked on open.

Fix: virtualize the move list (`@tanstack/react-virtual`) by flattening the tree to rows and rendering only what's visible. Open→interactive drops from ~9s to under half a second, and the number of mounted move cells goes from thousands to the hundreds.

Nested variation guides, per-variation collapse/expand, scroll-to-current-move, and the comments/variations/table toggles are all preserved. Adds unit tests for the flattening logic.

body: # Segmented Multi-Stream Synthesis & Dynamic Dashboard (Chunk 1.7.0) ## Summary This PR implements the Segmented Multi-Stream Synthesis pattern (ADR 005) to address LLM token ceiling limits and Serverless execution limits. It decouples the monolithic 11-dimension YouTube transcript analysis into 3 parallel concurrent requests, introduces database-level segment chunk persistence via `public.analysis_chunks`, performs auto-stitching in the `/persist` API upon completion of all chunks, and refactors the frontend stream adapter and Zustand store to dynamically reconstruct and render partial progress. ## Changes ### Database & Migrations - Added `supabase/migrations/20260613133000_add_analysis_chunks_table.sql` creating the `analysis_chunks` table with unique constraint on `(analysis_id, chunk_index)`. ### Domain, Ports, and Adapters (DDD / DI Alignment) - Updated `PersistencePort` and `SupabasePersistenceAdapter` to support `persistAnalysisChunk` and `findAnalysisChunks`. - Added `web/lib/utils/markdown-reconstructor.ts` for clean markdown layout rebuilding from structured JSON payload on both client and server. ### Backend Routing & Worker - Refactored `web/app/api/analyses/persist/route.ts` to support segmented chunk persistence, schema-based JSON validation, entity/relationship parsing, and auto-stitching. - Updated Cloudflare Worker (`worker/src/worker.ts`, `PromptBuilder.ts`, `ReasoningEnginePort.ts`) to receive and process explicit chunk segments. ### Client-Side Integration & State - Refactored `web/hooks/useSSEStream.ts` to initiate three concurrent streams in parallel. - Refactored `web/lib/adapters/synthesis-stream-adapter.ts` to progressively collect, heal, and reconstruct structured JSON segments. - Added `monetizationVerdict` state properties and `setMonetizationVerdict` action to `useSynthesisNucleus` store to fix compile-time type verification warnings. ## Gate Status - ✅ TypeScript compilation: `pnpm type-check` passed with 0 errors. - ✅ Lint checks: `pnpm lint` passed with 0 errors (warnings only). - ✅ Production build: `pnpm build` passed and bundled successfully. ## Verification & Architecture - Follows the Hex-Lite (Ports & Adapters) + DDD architectural patterns end-to-end. - Preserves the strict requirement for model cascades. ## Summary by Sourcery Implement segmented multi-stream analysis with chunked persistence and dynamic frontend reconstruction for YouTube transcript analyses. New Features: - Add database-backed analysis chunk storage and retrieval to support segmented analysis persistence. - Introduce three parallel LLM analysis streams and client-side handling for partial JSON segments with dynamic markdown regeneration. Bug Fixes: - Fix TypeScript typing gaps in the synthesis nucleus store by adding monetization verdict state and setter to align with the stream adapter. Enhancements: - Extend persistence APIs and worker contracts to handle chunk indices and stitch segmented payloads into a single validated analysis result. - Refactor the synthesis stream adapter and state store to progressively merge dimensions, track monetization verdicts, and avoid premature completion in partial streams. - Centralize markdown reconstruction from UCIS v2.0 JSON into a shared utility for consistent rendering across client and server. Documentation: - Add handover and review-matrix documents capturing the rollout, validation status, and review checkpoints for the multi-stream synthesis feature. Tests: - Document local gate status and CI-facing review matrix for the new multi-stream synthesis implementation. --- ## Summary by cubic Splits the 11-dimension analysis into three parallel streams, persists each chunk, and auto-stitches the final result to bypass token and serverless limits. The UI now streams partial results and rebuilds clean markdown in real time. - **New Features** - Segmented synthesis: three concurrent chunks (1–4, 5–8 + KG, 9–11 + classification + monetization). - Database chunk persistence via `public.analysis_chunks`; auto-stitching in `/api/analyses/persist` after all 3 complete with schema checks and KG writes. - Frontend SSE runs 3 streams in parallel; partial JSON is merged and markdown rebuilt via `reconstructMarkdown`. - Store/types: added `monetizationVerdict` and setter; completion fires only when all streams finish. - Worker: per-chunk prompts enforced; `chunkIndex` threaded through request, engine, and persist calls. - **Migration** - Run Supabase migration: `supabase/migrations/20260613133000_add_analysis_chunks_table.sql`. Written for commit 9c7ceabe59d475a71bb8c30a69c791bac31213af. Summary will update on new commits. ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **New Features** * Enabled parallel multi-stream analysis processing for improved performance and throughput * Added support for persistent chunk-based storage during analysis execution * Integrated monetization verdict tracking into analysis synthesis and output * **Chores** * Added test review matrix and technical handover documentation for release tracking

body:
This change replaces the single-page login demo with a production-style e-commerce foundation spanning storefront UX, account/order flows, and admin-facing capabilities. It introduces a secure backend API and deployment scaffolding aligned with the requested stack and feature set.

- **Frontend overhaul (single static app → full e-commerce experience)**
  - Reworked `index.html` into a multi-section storefront covering: Home, Shop, Product Details, Cart, Checkout, Auth, Dashboard, Wishlist, Order Tracking, Contact, About, FAQ, and Admin sections.
  - Added `styles.css` for responsive layouts (mobile/tablet/desktop), dark mode tokens, and motion/transition polish.
  - Added `app.js` for client state and interactions: product search/filter/sort/pagination, cart/wishlist persistence, coupon handling, checkout/order creation, tracking lookup, and auth form flows.

- **Backend API scaffold (Node/Express + MongoDB)**
  - Added `backend/` service with:
    - `src/models/index.js`: `User`, `Product`, `Order`, `Coupon` schemas.
    - `src/routes/index.js`: auth, product listing/filtering, order creation/history/tracking, admin analytics, payment intent endpoints.
    - `src/middleware/auth.js`: JWT auth + role guard.
    - `src/middleware/security.js`: rate limiting and security middleware composition.
    - `src/server.js`: app bootstrap, Mongo connection, API wiring.

- **Security baseline**
  - Implemented password hashing (bcrypt), JWT auth, CSRF token endpoint, input validation, rate limiting, helmet headers, XSS and NoSQL sanitization, and HPP protection.

- **Operational/docs updates**
  - Added `Dockerfile` and `docker-compose.yml` for local containerized deployment.
  - Replaced README with architecture, setup, API surface, security features, and deployment instructions.

```js
// backend/src/routes/index.js (excerpt)
router.post(
  '/auth/register',
  [
    body('name').trim().isLength({ min: 2 }),
    body('email').isEmail().normalizeEmail(),
    body('password').isLength({ min: 8 })
  ],
  validate,
  async (req, res) => {
    const hashedPassword = await bcrypt.hash(req.body.password, 12);
    const user = await User.create({ ...req.body, password: hashedPassword });
    const token = jwt.sign({ id: user.id, role: user.role }, process.env.JWT_SECRET, { expiresIn: '7d' });
    res.status(201).json({ token, user: { id: user.id, name: user.name, email: user.email } });
  }
);
```

author: gadzan
body:
## Summary The relay dashboard previously rendered all chat content as plain text in a `
`, so agent markdown (headings, bold, lists, code fences) showed as raw source. This renders agent output and the live streaming bubble as **sanitized markdown**, while keeping user input as plain text.

- **`src/lib/render-markdown.ts`** — `renderMarkdown(text, { streaming })`: `markdown-it` (`html:false`) → `DOMPurify` sanitize (defense-in-depth). Surviving links forced to `target=_blank rel="noopener noreferrer nofollow"`.
- **Streaming-safe**: with `streaming: true` the source is first run through [`remend`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/remend) (Vercel's zero-dep healing engine) to auto-close unterminated `**bold`, inline/fenced code, and partial links — so mid-stream frames don't swallow the rest of the message or show bare markers. Finalized text is not healed.
- **`src/components/StreamMarkdown.vue`** — `computed` + `v-html`, with non-scoped `.stream-md` styles (Tailwind preflight strips element styling for `v-html` content).
- **`MessageList.vue`** — `out` (agent) messages and the streaming bubble use `StreamMarkdown`; **`in` (user input) stays a plain `
`** — no markdown rendering, naturally XSS-inert.

### Security posture
- `html:false` escapes any raw HTML in the source; `DOMPurify` is a second pass over the rendered HTML.
- Covered by tests: raw `

body:
### Motivation
- Reframe the Daily Closing page from a dashboard-style view into a focused reconciliation screen for end-of-day verification.  
- Surface backend-imported / calculated totals so users primarily verify totals, enter counted cash, add notes, and optionally lock the day.  
- Improve mismatch visibility with accounting-oriented states (balanced, shortage, excess) while keeping the UI clean and non-decorative.  

### Description
- UI refactor: replace the previous layout with four clear sections: `Imported day summary`, `Cash reconciliation`, `Notes and day lock`, and `Closing history`, and add the helper text "Daily Closing verifies cash and business totals for the day. Billing and Daily Sales data are imported automatically." (modified `src/pages/DailyClosing.jsx`).  
- Add optional `opening_cash` support and show imported fields `expected_total`, `expected_cash`, `expenses`, `collected_amount`, and `outstanding` when available, falling back to calculated values otherwise (changes in `src/lib/dailyClosing.js`).  
- Calculation and normalization updates: `calculateClosing` now returns `openingCash`, `collectedAmount`, `outstanding`, along with `expectedCash`, `expectedTotal`, and `mismatch`, and `normalizeClosing` accepts common backend aliases for these fields; `closingPayload` only includes `opening_cash` when provided.  
- Visual improvements: compact accounting-oriented mismatch badge and container styles (subtle green for balanced, red for shortage, amber for excess), clearer badge text, an `Opening cash` optional input, and preserved behaviors for date selection, historical records, draft saves, and day locking (files changed: `src/pages/DailyClosing.jsx`, `src/lib/dailyClosing.js`, `src/lib/dailyClosing.test.js`).  

### Testing
- Ran unit tests with `npm test -- --watchAll=false src/lib/dailyClosing.test.js`, and all tests passed (`7 passed`).  
- Ran a production build with `npm run build`, which completed successfully; the build produced unrelated source-map and lint warnings (missing source maps in a third-party package, outdated Browserslist data, and some ESLint hook warnings in other pages) but the app compiled and the build output was generated.

body:
## What

Replaces the Nemotron local samples with a **Gemma 4 E4B QAT** sample as the recommended local default, plus a JetBrains Mellum 2 code-specialist sample.

- ➕ `samples/ollama-gemma4/` — default `unsloth/gemma-4-E4B-it-qat-GGUF:UD-Q4_K_XL`, claude-code runtime
- ➕ `samples/ollama-mellum2/` — JetBrains Mellum 2 (code specialist)
- ➖ delete `ollama-nemotron-4b` + `slack-nemotron-4b` (superseded)
- 🔁 e2e workflow builds `ollama-gemma4`; publish matrix: gemma4 → `-ollama`, mellum2 → `-mellum2`; `anthropic` stays `:latest` (zero-setup)
- 📝 root README + CLAUDE.md bug-pattern #4 updated

## Verified on an RTX 3080 (10 GB)

- claude-code → ollama → E4B QAT wrote **and ran** a Python script end-to-end in **~18 s** (Write + Bash, 3 turns), 100% on GPU
- Tool-calls 5/5 (single-shot + round-trip) for E2B/E4B/12B QAT over both `/api/chat` and the Anthropic `/v1/messages` path claude-code uses

## Findings baked into docs

- Gemma 4 needs **ollama ≥ 0.30.3** (the `gemma4` arch); older fails `unknown model architecture` → masquerades as `does not support tools`
- Pull unsloth QAT with the explicit **`:UD-Q4_K_XL`** tag (bare pull 400s — many GGUFs in the repo)
- Set **`OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH ≥ 32768`** so claude-code's ~30-50k-token prompt doesn't overflow ollama's 4096 default
- QAT (Q4_0) ~3× faster than regular Q4_K_M at 12B on a 10 GB card (less CPU spill); E4B stays 100% GPU even at 128k. MTP/Vulkan don't beat ollama's CUDA backend here.

author: fujiwara
body:
## What

Publish a second container image, tagged `:latest-dataplane` (and `:<version>-dataplane`), built from `Dockerfile.dataplane`. It bundles the [versitygw](https://github.com/versity/versitygw) S3 gateway and enables the Object Storage S3 data plane **by default** via env:

- `OBJECT_STORAGE_ENABLE_DATA_PLANE=true`
- `OBJECT_STORAGE_DATA_PLANE_ADDR=0.0.0.0:28086` (reachable on the published port)
- `OBJECT_STORAGE_DATA_PLANE_DIR=/data` (mount a volume to persist objects)

```bash
docker run --rm -p 18086:18086 -p 28086:28086 ghcr.io/sacloud/sakumock:latest-dataplane
aws --endpoint-url http://localhost:28086 s3 ls
```

The default `:latest` image is unchanged and stays lean (no versitygw).

## Why

versitygw is heavy, so bundling it into the default image would bloat it. A separate opt-in image gives a one-command S3 data plane for those who want it.

## Notes

- versitygw is fetched per target arch in a `--platform=$BUILDPLATFORM` build stage and only COPYed into the distroless final stage, so arm64 still builds without emulation (consistent with the existing COPY-only image).
- Verified locally: built the image, ran it, created a bucket via the control plane, and did S3 `ls`/`cp` (put+get) against the published `28086`.
